patents.title: Nucleic Acids Encoding Modified Chimeric Fusion Proteins
patents.abstract: What is disclosed herein are nucleic acids encoding a chimeric fusion protein comprising an extracellular domain that comprises an antigen binding domain, particularly a TROP2 binding domain. The nucleic acids disclosed here comprise codon-optimized coding sequence for the chimeric fusion protein and comprises a 5' UTR and a 3' UTR, wherein the 3' UTR comprises at least one microRNA binding site.
patents.assignee: CREATE MEDICINES INC [US]; CREATE MEDICINES, INC.
patents.novelty_summary: The patent discloses codon-optimized nucleic acids encoding chimeric fusion proteins with TROP2-binding extracellular domains and microRNA-responsive 3' UTRs for post-transcriptional regulation. This represents a composition-level innovation in controlling CAR construct expression through miRNA binding sites, potentially enabling tunable or tissue-specific CAR-T activation in vivo.

patents.title: COMPOSITIONS AND METHODS FOR ANTICANCER THERAPY
patents.abstract: Compositions comprising a nucleic acid for in vivo engineered cells, such as myeloid cells. The nucleic acid encodes a chimeric fusion protein that can be expressed predominantly on myeloid cells and has a binding domain capable to binding surface molecules on target cells such as cancer cells. Also disclosed are pharmaceutical compositions and methods for treating cancer.

patents.novelty_summary: This patent discloses nucleic acids designed for in vivo engineering of myeloid cells to express chimeric fusion proteins with tumor-targeting binding domains, representing a shift from traditional CAR-T approaches to CAR-myeloid cell engineering. The competitive significance lies in leveraging myeloid cells' innate immune properties and tissue infiltration capabilities as an alternative to T cell-based immunotherapy, potentially addressing limitations in CAR-T accessibility and efficacy in myeloid-rich tumor microenvironments.

patents.title: PARTITIONING ANION EXCHANGE CHROMATOGRAPHY FOR PURIFICATION OF RECOMBINANT ADENO-ASSOCIATED VIRUS (rAAV)
patents.abstract: [0000]    The present inventions provide methods for purifying adeno-associated viruses (AAV) that comprise gene of interest (GOI). The present inventions provide partitioning anion-exchange chromatography (AEX), leveraging surface charge differences between empty and full capsids to create an environment of on-column competition for binding sites. This results in empty capsids being removed during the column loading phase, allowing the bulk of full capsids to be eluted in a concentrated, highly enriched pool. The inventions also provide methods for conducting partitioning anion-exchange chromatography in rapid cycling mode for AAV purification process intensification.
patents.assignee: REGENERON PHARMA [US]; Regeneron Pharmaceuticals, Inc.
patents.novelty_summary: The patent presents a partitioning anion-exchange chromatography technique that exploits surface charge differences between empty and full AAV capsids to selectively remove empty capsids during column loading while concentrating full capsids in a single enriched pool. This represents a significant advancement in AAV purification efficiency and yield, which is critical for gene therapy manufacturing where empty capsid contamination reduces therapeutic efficacy and increases immunogenicity—a key bottleneck in scaling AAV-based gene therapy for in vivo applications.

patents.title: Surface-Modified Lipid Nanoparticles
patents.abstract: The disclosure provides conjugates comprising a targeting moiety, e.g., an antibody, Fab fragment or single chain variable fragment (ScFv), and a lipid nanoparticle (LNP) encapsulating a therapeutic agent (i.e., payload), wherein the targeting moiety, e.g., antibody, Fab fragment or the ScFv, is conjugated to the lipid nanoparticle through a linker, and wherein the linker comprises an enzyme recognition sequence such as a sortase recognition motif or a lipoic acid acceptor peptide. The disclosure further provides methods of preparing such conjugates.
patents.assignee: TESSERA THERAPEUTICS INC [US]; TESSERA THERAPEUTICS, INC.
patents.novelty_summary: The patent discloses surface-modified lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) with targeting moieties (antibodies, Fab, ScFv) conjugated via enzyme-cleavable linkers containing sortase or lipoic acid acceptor peptide motifs. This represents a novel approach to targeted LNP delivery with site-specific conjugation chemistry, potentially enabling more precise in vivo CAR-T cell targeting and reduced off-target effects through antibody-directed nanoparticle homing.
patents.title_original: NANOPARTICULES LIPIDIQUES MODIFIÉES EN SURFACE

patents.title: LIPID NANOPARTICLE METHODS AND COMPOSITIONS FOR PRODUCING GENETICALLY MODIFIED ERYTHROID CELLS
patents.abstract: Carriers such as lipid nanoparticles are useful for delivering payloads (such as RNA, DNA, proteins, or small molecules) to cells such as erythroid cells. This disclosure provides improved carriers that comprise a targeting agent that binds a cell surface receptor. In some embodiments, the cell surface receptor is one that undergoes a high rate of endocytosis.
patents.assignee: TESSERA THERAPEUTICS INC [US]; Tessera Therapeutics, Inc.
patents.novelty_summary: The patent discloses lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) incorporating targeting agents that bind cell surface receptors undergoing high-rate endocytosis, specifically for delivery to erythroid cells. The competitive significance lies in improved cellular uptake efficiency and specificity for non-lymphoid cell populations, which could expand the therapeutic scope beyond CAR-T to red blood cell engineering and other cell therapy modalities.
patents.title_original: LIPIDNANOPARTIKELVERFAHREN UND ZUSAMMENSETZUNGEN ZUR HERSTELLUNG VON GENTECHNISCH VERÄNDERTEN ERYTHROIDZELLEN

patents.title: DRUG CONJUGATES WITH LIPID NANOPARTICLES
patents.abstract: The disclosure provides conjugates comprising a targeting moiety, e.g., an antibody, Fab fragment or single chain variable fragment (ScFv), and a lipid nanoparticle (LNP) encapsulating a therapeutic agent (i.e., payload), wherein the targeting moiety, e.g., antibody, Fab fragment or the ScFv, is conjugated to the lipid nanoparticle through a linker, and wherein the linker comprises an enzyme recognition sequence and a Click product formed from a Click reaction between a first Click handle on the targeting moiety, e.g., antibody, Fab fragment, or ScFv, and a second Click handle on the LNP.
patents.assignee: TESSERA THERAPEUTICS INC [US]; TESSERA THERAPEUTICS, INC.
patents.novelty_summary: The patent describes a novel conjugate architecture combining antibody/protein targeting moieties with lipid nanoparticles via enzyme-cleavable linkers formed through Click chemistry. This dual-targeting approach enables both cell-specific delivery and triggered payload release, offering competitive advantage for in vivo CAR-T applications by potentially improving trafficking to tumor sites and controlled therapeutic payload release in T cells or antigen-presenting cells.
patents.title_original: CONJUGUÉS MÉDICAMENTEUX À NANOPARTICULES LIPIDIQUES

patents.title: TRANSFECTION EXTRACORPORELLE DE CELLULES EFFECTRICES IMMUNITAIRES
patents.abstract: Methods for extracorporeal transfection of an immune effector cell are provided. The method includes contacting blood, or a cell-containing fraction thereof, from a subject with a nanoparticle. The nanoparticle includes a surface-exposed immune effector binding moiety. Furthermore, the nanoparticle includes a nucleic acid encoding a chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) or T-cell receptor (TCR).
patents.assignee: NANOCELL THERAPEUTICS HOLDINGS B V [NL]; NANOCELL THERAPEUTICS HOLDINGS B.V.
patents.novelty_summary: The patent presents a nanoparticle-based platform for extracorporeal transfection of immune effector cells using surface-exposed binding moieties to target and deliver CAR or TCR-encoding nucleic acids directly ex vivo. This approach offers potential competitive advantages over conventional electroporation or viral vector methods by enabling direct cell targeting, potentially improving transfection efficiency and cell viability while simplifying the manufacturing process for CAR-T and TCR-engineered cell therapies.

patents.title: Methods and Composition for Inducing Activation and Expression of DNA in T Lymphocytes
patents.abstract: The disclosure relates to nanoparticles comprising a surface-exposed immune cell binding moiety, a transposable element comprising a gene sequence flanked by inverted terminal repeats (ITRs), a nucleic acid encoding a transposase with specificity for the ITRs, and an mRNA encoding a first chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) or T-cell receptor (TCR). Methods are also described for treating a disease or disorder by administering such nanoparticles to a subject in need thereof.
patents.assignee: NANOCELL THERAPEUTICS HOLDINGS B V [NL]; NANOCELL THERAPEUTICS HOLDINGS B.V.
patents.novelty_summary: The patent describes nanoparticles with surface-binding moieties that co-deliver transposable elements (with transposase), mRNA encoding CAR/TCR, and regulatory sequences to T lymphocytes for direct in vivo activation and transgene expression. This combines non-viral nanoparticle delivery with transposon-mediated integration and mRNA-based CAR/TCR expression, offering potential advantages in avoiding viral vectors and enabling rapid ex vivo or in vivo T cell engineering without requiring cell extraction.
patents.title_original: MÉTHODES ET COMPOSITION POUR INDUIRE L'ACTIVATION ET L'EXPRESSION D'ADN DANS DES LYMPHOCYTES T

patents.title: Methods and Compositions for Administering a Nucleic Acid Construct
patents.abstract: The present disclosure includes a composition including a) one or more nucleic acid constructs, wherein the one or more nucleic acid constructs encode: at least one of Replicase 68 (Rep68) and Replicase 78 (Rep78); and at least one protein of viral origin having nucleic acid replication and/or transgene amplification promotion activity, and b) nucleic acid construct comprising a coding region encoding at least one gene of interest (GOI) and at least one inverted terminal repeat (ITR) sequence on each side of the GOI, and methods of making and using the composition.
patents.assignee: NANOCELL THERAPEUTICS HOLDINGS B V [NL]; NANOCELL THERAPEUTICS HOLDINGS B.V.
patents.novelty_summary: The invention combines Rep68/Rep78 replicases with viral proteins that enhance nucleic acid replication and transgene amplification within a self-complementary AAV-like system (ITR-flanked GOI construct). This represents a novel approach to enhance transgene expression levels and persistence in vivo, potentially offering improved efficacy for CAR-T and other gene therapy applications through synergistic amplification of the delivered genetic material.
patents.title_original: PROCÉDÉS ET COMPOSITIONS POUR ADMINISTRER UNE CONSTRUCTION NUCLÉIQUE

patents.title: MEANS AND METHODS FOR ADMINISTERING AGENTS TO IMMUNE EFFECTOR CELLS
patents.abstract: The current disclosure relates to targeted delivery of agents to T cells and/or NK cells. Highly suitable targeting domains were meticulously identified that allow for an agent, such as DNA and/or RNA, to be delivered to T cells and/or NK cells. As shown, when lipid nanoparticles were provided with such a targeting domain, nucleic acid comprised in said lipid nanoparticles was highly efficiently and specifically delivered. This allows for engineering of T cells and/or NK cells, highly useful in medical treatments for cancer.
patents.assignee: NANOCELL THERAPEUTICS HOLDINGS B V [NL]; NANOCELL THERAPEUTICS HOLDINGS B.V.
patents.novelty_summary: The patent discloses targeted lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) with novel targeting domains specifically engineered for efficient and selective delivery of nucleic acids (DNA/RNA) to T cells and NK cells. This addresses a key challenge in cell engineering therapies by improving transfection specificity and efficiency, which is strategically significant for in vivo CAR-T applications where off-target delivery limits therapeutic efficacy and safety.
patents.title_original: MOYENS ET MÉTHODES D'ADMINISTRATION D'AGENTS À DES CELLULES EFFECTRICES IMMUNITAIRES

patents.title: VIRAL VECTORS WITH INTEGRATION AND SELF-INACTIVATION AND CONSTRUCTIONS AND USES THEREOF
patents.abstract: The present disclosure relates to gene delivery systems and methods of producing and using single constructs or viral vectors that carry a transposon and a transposase gene that is functional in target cells and not functional in producer cells.
patents.assignee: NANOCELL THERAPEUTICS B V [NL]; NANOCELL THERAPEUTICS B.V.
patents.novelty_summary: The patent discloses dual-function viral vectors carrying both a transposon and a transposase gene with differential activity—functional in target cells but inactive in producer cells—enabling self-inactivating gene delivery systems. This addresses a key challenge in ex vivo cell engineering by preventing transposase activity during vector production while enabling efficient integration post-transduction, with potential significance for CAR-T manufacturing where controlled, safe gene integration is critical.
patents.title_original: VECTEURS VIRAUX À INTÉGRATION ET À AUTO-INACTIVATION ET CONSTRUCTIONS ET UTILISATIONS DE CEUX-CI

patents.title: Systems and Methods for Concentrating Populations of Sorted Cells
patents.abstract: Provided herein are devices, systems, and methods for sorting, concentrating, and dispensing a single particle or a small number of particles from a sample in a continuous, integrated workflow to facilitate downstream particle analysis. Such methods, devices, and systems can be used to identify, sort, change the particle concentration, and dispense a subset of particles or a single particle from a sample into a well in a multi-well plate or strip. Using microfluidics and acoustic field technologies to perform particle sorting, concentrating, and dispensing in a single device or system allows for streamlining the steps into a continuous, integrated process as compared to traditional flow cytometry systems.
patents.assignee: NANOCELLECT BIOMEDICAL INC [US]; NANOCELLECT BIOMEDICAL, INC.
patents.title_original: SYSTÈMES ET PROCÉDÉS DE CONCENTRATION DE POPULATIONS DE CELLULES TRIÉES

patents.title: SYSTEMES MICROFLUIDIQUES ET PROCEDES DE TRI DE PARTICULES
patents.abstract:
[0001]    Provided herein are devices, systems, and methods for particle sorting, including cell sorting, using microfluidics cartridges and microchips and the manufacture of the microfluidics cartridges and microchips by high-throughput approaches. Such methods, devices, and systems can be used to identify, sort, and collect a subset of particles or a single particle from a sample. The capability to manufacture such microfluidic tools in high volume may lower production costs and allow for the microfluidic tools to be used as consumables.
[0002]    L'invention concerne des dispositifs, des systèmes et des procédés de tri de particules, comprenant le tri de cellules, à l'aide de cartouches microfluidiques et de micropuces et la fabrication des cartouches microfluidiques et des micropuces par des approches à haut débit. De tels procédés, dispositifs et systèmes peuvent être utilisés pour identifier, trier et collecter un sous-ensemble de particules ou une particule unique à partir d'un
patents.assignee: NANOCELLECT BIOMEDICAL INC [US]; NANOCELLECT BIOMEDICAL, INC.
patents.novelty_summary: The patent describes microfluidic devices and high-throughput manufacturing methods for particle/cell sorting, with potential application to cell therapy manufacturing. The competitive significance lies in enabling cost-effective, consumable-grade microfluidic tools that could streamline cell selection processes in CAR-T manufacturing pipelines, though the patent itself does not specifically disclose CAR-T engineering or genetic modification.

patents.title: Polysaccharide core Nanocells as well as preparation method and application thereof
patents.abstract: The invention discloses polysaccharide core Nanocells as well as a preparation method and application thereof. Each polysaccharide core Nanocell is of a core-shell structure, a nanoparticle made of a polysaccharide material serve as a core, the outer layer of the nanoparticle is wrapped with a lipid membrane which is formed by a lipid material and similar to a lipidosome capsule membrane, and a medicine is entrapped in the nanoparticle, and/or between the lipid membrane and the nanoparticle core, and/or entrapped on the lipid membrane. According to the polysaccharide core Nanocells, different lipid materials can be adopted, or lipid is modified with different targeting guide molecules, and magnetic particles are wrapped or materials or medicines sensitive to the microenvironment of a corresponding disease site are added, so that the polysaccharide core Nanocell with different targeting functions is obtained; medicines of various mechanisms can be simultaneously entrapped, so that multi
patents.assignee: UNIV JINAN; 暨南大学
patents.novelty_summary: The patent discloses a core-shell nanoparticle design with a polysaccharide core wrapped in a lipid membrane, enabling drug/therapeutic cargo encapsulation with tunable targeting via modified lipids and magnetic properties. While this represents a novel nanoparticle architecture, its specific application to CAR-T cell delivery or in vivo CAR-T therapy is not explicitly detailed in the provided abstract, limiting assessment of competitive significance for that therapeutic modality.

patents.title: COMPOSITIONS AND METHODS FOR MODULATING T LYMPHOCYTES
patents.abstract: The present disclosure provides compositions and methods for delivering an engineered immune receptor to immune cells, e.g., T cells, in vivo, ex vivo, or in vitro. Provided are recombinant nucleic acids and templates that are useful for immune cell reprogramming with high specificity and efficiency.
patents.assignee: AVERNA THERAPEUTICS LTD [IL]; AVERNA THERAPEUTICS LTD
patents.novelty_summary: The patent discloses recombinant nucleic acids and templates for delivering engineered immune receptors to T cells across multiple delivery contexts (in vivo, ex vivo, in vitro) with claimed high specificity and efficiency. The competitive significance for in vivo CAR-T relates to improved delivery mechanisms and reprogramming efficiency that could enhance therapeutic potency while potentially reducing off-target effects.
patents.title_original: COMPOSITIONS ET MÉTHODES DE MODULATION DE LYMPHOCYTES T

patents.title: Engineered retrotransposable element proteins for gene delivery and insertion
patents.abstract: The present disclosure provides compositions and methods for enhancing the integration of a transgene into a genome.
patents.assignee: AVERNA THERAPEUTICS LTD [IL]; AVERNA THERAPEUTICS LTD.
patents.novelty_summary: The patent describes engineered retrotransposable element proteins as a novel gene delivery and genomic integration platform, potentially offering an alternative to viral vectors for stable transgene insertion. This could provide competitive advantages for ex vivo T cell engineering by enabling safer, non-viral integration of CAR and TCR constructs with reduced immunogenicity and manufacturing complexity compared to lentiviral or AAV systems.

patents.title: Recombinant proteins comprising non-ltr retrotransposon-derived polypeptides for gene delivery and insertion
patents.assignee: AVERNA THERAPEUTICS LTD [IL]; TRUDEAU DEVIN [IL]; BEN SHUSHAN GOLECZKI YARON [IL]
patents.novelty_summary: The patent describes recombinant proteins engineered from non-LTR retrotransposon-derived polypeptides for gene delivery and insertion applications. This represents a novel approach to intracellular gene delivery using endogenous retrotransposon machinery, offering potential advantages over viral vectors in terms of immunogenicity and manufacturing scalability for cell and gene therapy applications.

patents.title: COMPOSITIONS FOR TARGET-PRIMED REVERSE TRANSCRIPTION
patents.abstract: Provided herein are nucleic acid constructs and systems for target primed reverse transcription gene insertion. The constructs and systems may comprise a non-naturally occurring nucleic acid molecule comprising a 3' UTR sequence comprising a mutation relative to a wild-type R2 3' UTR sequence.
patents.assignee: ADDITION THERAPEUTICS INC [US]; ADDITION THERAPEUTICS, INC.
patents.novelty_summary: The patent discloses engineered nucleic acid constructs with mutated 3' UTR sequences derived from R2 retrotransposons, optimized for target-primed reverse transcription (TPRT)-mediated gene insertion. This represents a novel approach to improving gene integration efficiency, which could enhance in vivo CAR-T applications by enabling more efficient and precise transgene delivery without viral vectors.
patents.title_original: COMPOSITIONS POUR LA TRANSCRIPTION INVERSE AMORCÉE PAR LA CIBLE

patents.title: RNA TAILS FOR TARGET-PRIMED REVERSE TRANSCRIPTION
patents.abstract: Provided herein are nucleic acid constructs and systems for target primed reverse transcription gene insertion.
patents.assignee: ADDITION THERAPEUTICS INC [US]; ADDITION THERAPEUTICS, INC.
patents.novelty_summary: The patent describes nucleic acid constructs designed for target-primed reverse transcription (TPRT)-mediated gene insertion, representing a delivery mechanism distinct from conventional viral vectors. This technology could enable efficient in vivo integration of therapeutic transgenes including CAR-T constructs with reduced immunogenicity and improved safety profiles compared to lentiviral or adeno-associated viral approaches.
patents.title_original: QUEUES D'ARN POUR TRANSCRIPTION INVERSE AMORCÉE CIBLE

patents.title: NUCLEIC ACID INSERTION IN YOUNG MAMMALS
patents.abstract: Provided herein are methods and systems for modifying a target nucleic acid in a cell of a subject. The methods and systems may comprise providing the cell with a first nucleic acid comprising (i) a 5' untranslated region (UTR) sequence and a 3' untranslated region (UTR) sequence, and (ii) a template sequence. The methods and systems may further comprise providing the cell with an R2 retroelement polypeptide or a second nucleic acid encoding the R2 retroelement polypeptide. The R2 retroelement polypeptide may insert the template sequence or a reverse complement thereof into the target nucleic acid. The subject may be a mammal less than 6 weeks of age.
patents.assignee: ADDITION THERAPEUTICS INC [US]; GREGOIRE FRANCINE M [US]; UPTON HEATHER [US]
patents.novelty_summary: This patent describes a novel nucleic acid insertion technology using R2 retroelement polypeptides to precisely integrate template sequences into target genomic loci in young mammals (under 6 weeks). The competitive significance for in vivo CAR-T is potentially high, as this retroelement-based integration approach could enable efficient, site-specific transgene insertion in developing T cells without requiring ex vivo cell manipulation, complementing or competing with current lentiviral and transposon-based CAR-T manufacturing platforms.
patents.title_original: INSERTION D'ACIDE NUCLÉIQUE CHEZ DES JEUNES MAMMIFÈRES

patents.title: Multi-Component Systems for Site-Specific Genomic Modifications
patents.abstract: Provided herein are genome editing systems comprising a reverse transcriptase and a template RNA with a translation-incapable 5' cap (TI-CAP) encoding a payload. The genome editing systems can be used to target, edit, modify, or manipulate a DNA sequence at one or more locations in a safe harbor site of the genome of a cell.
patents.assignee: ADDITION THERAPEUTICS INC [US]; ADDITION THERAPEUTICS, INC.
patents.novelty_summary: This patent describes genome editing systems combining reverse transcriptase with a novel translation-incapable 5' cap (TI-CAP) template RNA to enable site-specific genomic modifications at safe harbor loci. The TI-CAP architecture represents a novel approach to controlling payload delivery while preventing unwanted translation, offering competitive advantage for precise, safer integration of therapeutic payloads (including CAR-T constructs) into predefined genomic safe harbor sites.
patents.title_original: SYSTÈMES À COMPOSANTS MULTIPLES POUR MODIFICATIONS GÉNOMIQUES SPÉCIFIQUES À UN SITE

patents.title: STIMULATOR OF INTERFERON GENE MODULATORS (STING) AND THEIR USES
patents.abstract: Compounds of the present invention act as stimulator of interferon genes (STING) pathway modulators and are useful in the treatment of a variety of clinical conditions in which uncontrolled growth and spread of abnormal cells occurs, in addition to microbial infections, controlling pathogenic cGAS activity, neurodegeneration, associated autoimmune diseases, inflammatory diseases, neuropathic pain and vaccine adjuvants. The compounds have the following formulae I-IV: (I), (II), (III) and (IV).
patents.assignee: LONDON PHARMACEUTICALS AND RES CORPORATION [CA]; LONDON PHARMACEUTICALS AND RESEARCH CORPORATION
patents.novelty_summary: Novel STING pathway modulators with broad therapeutic applications including cancer, infections, and immune modulation. While STING agonists have known immunostimulatory properties, the specific chemical compounds claimed (formulae I-IV) and their potency as STING modulators represent the patent's novelty; this is competitively significant for in vivo CAR-T as STING activation can enhance anti-tumor immunity and synergize with cellular therapies.
patents.title_original: STIMULATEUR DE MODULATEURS DE GÈNES D'INTERFÉRON (STING) ET LEURS UTILISATIONS

patents.title: ANTIGENBINDENDE POLYPEPTIDE GEGEN CD229
patents.abstract: The invention relates to antigen-binding polypeptides comprising the CDR1, CDR2 and CDR3 region of a VHH domain of a camelid heavy chain antibody. The polypeptides bind specifically to CD229 and are therefore suitable for the diagnosis as well as for the therapeutic and prophylactic treatment of diseases characterised by increased CD229 expression. Fusion proteins, conjugates and pharmaceutical compositions comprising the antigen-binding polypeptides are also disclosed. In addition, the invention relates to the use of such antigen-binding polypeptides in methods for detecting CD229 or CD229-expressing cells in a biological sample. Methods for purifying and concentrating CD229 or CD229-expressing cells using the antigen-binding polypeptides are also described.
patents.assignee: UNIV HAMBURG EPPENDORF [DE]; Universitätsklinikum Hamburg-Eppendorf
patents.novelty_summary: The invention discloses novel VHH-based antigen-binding polypeptides targeting CD229 with defined CDR regions from camelid heavy chain antibodies, along with fusion proteins and conjugates for therapeutic use. This is relevant to CAR-T engineering as CD229 is an emerging target on B-cell malignancies and lymphomas, and nanobody-based binding domains offer compact alternatives to scFv for CAR construct optimization.

patents.title: METHOD AND APPARATUS FOR SORTING AND CULTURING CELLS, COMPUTING DEVICE AND STORAGE MEDIUM
patents.abstract: The present application relates to the technical field of biomedicine. Provided are a cell sorting and culturing method and apparatus, a computer device, and a storage medium. The cell sorting and culturing method comprises separating a sample solution by means of a density gradient centrifugation method to obtain a cell solution to be cultured; conveying said cell solution to a culturing device by means of a first pipeline switching operation, and culturing said cell solution to obtain a cultured cell solution; and acquiring the cultured cell solution by means of a second pipeline switching operation, and concentrating and washing the cultured cell solution to obtain a target cell solution. The cell sorting and culturing method can ensure a fully enclosed one-stop sterile operating environment, avoid the risk of contamination during cell operation site changing, and improve the cell treatment stability. In addition, continuous operation between cell solution sorting and culturing trea
patents.assignee: BEIJING CELLBRI FUTURE BIOTECHNOLOGY CO LTD [CN]; 北京赛桥未来生物科技有限公司
patents.novelty_summary: The patent describes an automated, fully enclosed pipeline system for cell sorting via density gradient centrifugation, culture, concentration, and washing in a sterile environment. The competitive significance for in vivo CAR-T lies in streamlined ex vivo cell manufacturing with reduced contamination risk and improved process reproducibility, potentially enabling faster turnaround for autologous CAR-T production.
patents.title_original: PROCÉDÉ ET APPAREIL DE TRI ET DE CULTURE DE CELLULES, DISPOSITIF INFORMATIQUE ET SUPPORT DE STOCKAGE

patents.title: ADDITIFS POUR LA PRODUCTION DE VECTEURS VIRAUX
patents.abstract: Among other things, the present disclosure provides methods, systems, and compositions for production of viral vectors, e.g., recombinant viral vectors, e.g., recombinant adeno-associated viruses (rAAVs). In some embodiments, a method comprises addition of one or more additives to a medium comprising host cells. In some embodiments, an addition of an additive to a medium can provide increased titer of produced recombinant viral vector particles, e.g., rAAV particles. In some embodiments, an additive comprises momelotinib or a salt or derivative thereof.
patents.assignee: BIOGEN MA INC [US]; BIOGEN MA INC.
patents.novelty_summary: The patent discloses additives (specifically momelotinib and derivatives) added to cell culture media to increase titer of recombinant viral vector production, particularly rAAV. This addresses a critical manufacturing bottleneck for viral vector-based gene therapy by improving production efficiency, which is significant for cost-effective scale-up of in vivo CAR-T delivery systems utilizing AAV vectors.

patents.title: PEPTIDES BINDING TO GRPR
patents.abstract: Described herein are GRPR binding peptides having the structure: R1-R2-dPhe-Gln-Trp-Ala-Val-Gly-His-Leu-R3 (SEQ. ID. NO: 1) wherein R1 is absent or is a chelator moiety, optionally bound to a radioactive atom moiety; R2 is absent or is a linker; and R3 is a N- (thiomethyl) alkyl-glycine residue having the structure: (I) wherein n is between 1 and 5; and R4 is H, methyl, ethyl, or propyl. In addition, methods for diagnosis and treatment of disease, in particular cancer, using compositions comprising GRPR binding peptides are disclosed.
patents.assignee: STARGET PHARMA LTD [IL]; STARGET PHARMA LTD
patents.novelty_summary: Novel GRPR-binding peptides with modular structure enabling radioisotope conjugation (via chelator moiety at R1) and flexible linker/C-terminal modifications. Significant for in vivo CAR-T delivery: GRPR targeting enables tumor-homing imaging and potential radioimmunotherapy; modular design allows adaptation to CAR-T cell surface display or dual-targeting constructs for enhanced tumor localization and reduced systemic toxicity in cell therapy applications.
patents.title_original: PEPTIDES SE LIANT À GRPR

patents.title: REPEATED DOSAGE OF RETROTRANSPOSONS
patents.abstract: The present disclosure demonstrates that earlier editing of cells with ribosomal non-LTR retrotransposons (R elements) still allowed sufficient editing from subsequent dosing of R elements, without significant interference therebetween, whether they are the same R elements or different. Provided are compositions and methods for integrating one or more exogenous sequence(s) to the genome of a mammalian cell, comprising (a) introducing to the cell a first amount of one or more polynucleotide(s) comprising a first ribosomal non-long terminal repeat (LTR) retrotransposon (R element) which comprises a first exogenous sequence, and, (b) introducing to the cell a second amount of one or more polynucleotide(s) comprising a second R element.
patents.assignee: TYPEWRITER THERAPEUTICS INC [US]; UNIV TOKYO [JP]; TYPEWRITER THERAPEUTICS, INC.
patents.novelty_summary: The patent demonstrates that repeated dosing of non-LTR retrotransposons (R elements) for genome editing can be performed sequentially without significant interference, whether using identical or different R elements. This is significant for in vivo CAR-T applications as it enables multi-step genetic modifications and stacked transgene integration, potentially allowing more complex therapeutic payloads or iterative optimization of CAR constructs through sequential editing events.
patents.title_original: DOSAGE RÉPÉTÉ DE RÉTROTRANSPOSONS

patents.title: New R2 Retrotransposons for Gene Writing
patents.abstract: The present disclosure describes numerous new R2 retrotransposons discovered from various species. These R2 retrotransposons exhibited good retrotransposition activities in human cells. These new retrotransposons, as well as engineered versions thereof, can be suitably used for targeted gene delivery.
patents.assignee: TYPEWRITER THERAPEUTICS INC [US]; TYPEWRITER THERAPEUTICS, INC.
patents.novelty_summary: The patent discloses novel R2 retrotransposons from various species with demonstrated retrotransposition activity in human cells, engineered for targeted gene delivery applications. While R2 retrotransposons represent an alternative to viral vectors and integrating transposons, their specific advantage for in vivo CAR-T applications is unclear without claim-level detail on targeting specificity or T cell transduction efficiency.
patents.title_original: NOUVEAUX RÉTROTRANSPOSONS R2 POUR L'ÉCRITURE GÉNIQUE

patents.title: R2 RETROTRANSPOSONS FOR GENE WRITING
patents.abstract: The present disclosure describes new R2 retrotransposons discovered from bird species. Two of them, from Corvus moneduloides (New Caledonian crow) and Accipiter gentilis (Eurasian goshawk) and referred to as R2Cm and R2Ag, respectively, exhibited excellent retrotransposition activities in human cells. These new retrotransposons, as well as engineered versions thereof, can be suitably used for targeted gene delivery.
patents.assignee: TYPEWRITER THERAPEUTICS INC [US]; UNIV TOKYO [JP]; TYPEWRITER THERAPEUTICS, INC.
patents.novelty_summary: Novel R2 retrotransposons derived from bird species (Corvus moneduloides and Accipiter gentilis) with enhanced retrotransposition activity in human cells, engineered for targeted gene delivery applications. This represents a differentiated delivery vehicle technology for gene therapy that could provide an alternative to viral vectors with potential advantages in specificity and immunogenicity profile.
patents.title_original: RÉTROTRANSPOSONS R2 POUR L'ÉCRITURE GÉNIQUE

patents.title: FUSION PROTEIN INTENDED TO BE USED AS AN IMMUNE CELL ENGAGER
patents.abstract: Disclosed herein are immune cell engagers. The immune cell engager may include a cell binding domain, an immune cell adhesion molecule, an immune cell costimulatory molecule, or a combination thereof. Methods of use and production are further provided.
patents.assignee: UMOJA BIOPHARMA INC [US]; UMOJA BIOPHARMA, INC.
patents.novelty_summary: The patent discloses fusion proteins functioning as immune cell engagers with modular domains combining cell binding, adhesion, and costimulatory functions. This represents a novel approach to redirecting and activating T cells without requiring TCR or CAR genetic engineering, positioning it as a potential alternative or complementary technology to traditional CAR-T for in vivo immune cell engagement and activation.
patents.title_original: PROTÉINE DE FUSION DESTINÉE À ÊTRE UTILISÉE EN TANT QU'ENGAGEUR DE CELLULES IMMUNITAIRES

patents.title: Multispecific Activator of Immune Cells and Its Uses
patents.abstract: Provided here are immune cell engagers and multispecific immune cell engagers. Some such embodiments include an adhesion molecule linked to a costimulatory molecule or an immune cell binding domain and a target cell binding domain. The disclosure also includes vectors such as lentiviral vectors, cells, and methods that may relate to or include such engagers. The multispecific immune cell engagers may incorporate a fusion molecule comprising a CD58 extracellular domain, an anti-CD3 antibody, a CD80 or CD86 extracellular domain, and a target cell binding domain.
patents.assignee: UMOJA BIOPHARMA INC [US]; UMOJA BIOPHARMA, INC.
patents.novelty_summary: The patent discloses multispecific immune cell engagers incorporating adhesion molecules (CD58), costimulatory domains (CD80/CD86), anti-CD3 binding, and target cell binding domains in a single fusion molecule, combined with lentiviral vector delivery and engineered cell compositions. This represents a novel approach to enhance T cell activation and targeting specificity by combining multiple immunomodulatory signals in trans, potentially improving CAR-T efficacy and reducing off-target toxicity through integrated costimulation.
patents.title_original: ACTIVATEUR MULTISPÉCIFIQUE DES CELLULES IMMUNITAIRES ET SES UTILISATIONS

patents.title: FABRICATION DE PARTICULES VIRALES
patents.abstract: Provided are methods for large scale production of viral particles, and compositions and methods for using said viral particles.

patents.title: Receptor Targeting a Gate-Controlled Adapter
patents.abstract: Provided are compositions and methods for polynucleotides and vectors encoding novel chimeric receptor systems. The Gated Adaptor Targeting Receptor (GATR) system employs a dual adaptor system: a first, targeting adaptor and a second, gating adaptor. The targeting adaptor bispecifically binds both the target cell and the gating adaptor, while an engineered cell expressing the chimeric receptor binds the gating adaptor. This targets the engineered cells to an antigen recognized by the targeting adaptor thereby activating the engineered cells and leading to the desired physiological effect.
patents.assignee: UMOJA BIOPHARMA INC [US]; UMOJA BIOPHARMA, INC.
patents.novelty_summary: The GATR (Gated Adaptor Targeting Receptor) system introduces a dual adaptor architecture for engineered cell targeting: a bispecific targeting adaptor that bridges tumor antigen recognition with a gating adaptor, while engineered cells express complementary chimeric receptors. This dual-adaptor gating mechanism offers potential competitive advantages for in vivo CAR-T by enabling improved specificity, reduced off-target activation, and potentially reversible targeting through adaptor modulation.
