patents.assignee: 科済生物医薬（上海）有限公司ＣＡＲＳＧＥＮ  ＴＨＥＲＡＰＥＵＴＩＣＳ  ＣＯ．，ＬＴＤ．; 上海市腫瘍研究所ＳＨＡＮＧＨＡＩ  ＣＡＮＣＥＲ  ＩＮＳＴＩＴＵＴＥ
patents.novelty_summary: This patent describes binding units specifically targeting FAP-α (fibroblast activation protein alpha) for use in immunotherapy, along with nucleotides encoding these units and their incorporation into vectors and host cells. The competitive significance lies in FAP-α being a tumor-associated antigen expressed on cancer-associated fibroblasts, and the patent demonstrates that immune effector cells (likely CAR-T cells) containing these binding units exhibit significant cytotoxic capability against FAP-α-expressing tumor cells, potentially enabling dual-targeting strategies in solid tumors.
patents.title_original: 線維芽細胞活性化タンパク質αを標的とする結合ユニットとその応用

patents.title: Method for improving immune response cell function
patents.abstract: The invention relates to a method for improving the function of immune response cells. The invention discloses an immune response cell which expresses at least one receptor capable of binding to an antigen and type I interferon. The immune response cell is applied to treatment of tumors, infectious diseases and other diseases, and has remarkable and excellent capability of killing tumors or pathogens.
patents.assignee: CARSGEN THERAPEUTICS SHANGHAI CO LTD; 科济生物医药（上海）有限公司; 恺兴生命科技（上海）有限公司
patents.novelty_summary: The patent describes immune response cells engineered to co-express antigen-binding receptors (likely CAR or TCR) alongside type I interferon production, targeting enhanced tumor and pathogen killing. This dual-expression approach aims to overcome immunosuppressive tumor microenvironments through endogenous IFN-I signaling, representing a potentially competitive enhancement to standard CAR-T therapy for in vivo efficacy.

patents.title: Pseudotyped Viral Particle and Its Use
patents.abstract: A pseudotyped viral particle having a Maraba virus envelope glycoprotein or a variant thereof. The surface of the pseudotyped virus envelope comprises an immune cell targeting molecule and/or an immune cell activating molecule. A corresponding targeting molecule is designed according to a cell receptor to be targeted, and can target different types of cells, including immunotherapy cells such as CAR-T and CAR-NK.
patents.assignee: SHENZHEN IMMUNOFOCO BIOTECHNOLOGY CO LTD [CN]; SHANGHAI IMMUNOFOCO PHARMACEUTICAL RES CO LTD [CN]; CHENGDU IMMUNOFOCO BIOTECHNOLOGY CO LTD [CN]
patents.novelty_summary: The patent discloses pseudotyped viral particles using Maraba virus envelope glycoproteins decorated with immune cell targeting and/or activating molecules on the surface, enabling selective delivery to immunotherapy cells including CAR-T and CAR-NK. The competitive significance lies in providing a non-integrating viral vector platform for targeted transduction of engineered T cells, potentially improving CAR-T manufacturing efficiency and reducing off-target effects during ex vivo engineering.
patents.title_original: PARTICULE VIRALE PSEUDOTYPÉE ET SON UTILISATION

patents.title: METHOD FOR PREDICTING A TREATMENT RESPONSE TO IMMUNOCELLULAR THERAPY FOR SOLID TUMORS
patents.abstract: The present invention relates to a method for predicting a solid tumor immune cell therapy treatment response. The method comprises acquiring a tumor tissue section from a patient, and detecting the presence, number, proportion or density of one or more cell types in the tumor tissue section. A solid tumor immune cell therapy response is predicted by determining cell markers, such as α-SMA, CD3, CD4 or CD8, associated with the cell types. In addition, the present invention also relates to a kit used for predicting a solid tumor treatment response, including a reagent which detects expression levels of one or more cell types and cell markers in tumor tissue sections, and software and/or a user manual used for analyzing detection results. The method and kit provide an effective tool for clinical treatment, so as to optimize dosages and clinical regimens of immune cell therapy, thereby improving treatment response rates.
patents.assignee: SUZHOU IMMUNOFOCO BIOTECHNOLOGY CO LTD [CN]; SHANGHAI IMMUNOFOCO PHARMACEUTICAL RES CO LTD [CN]; CHENGDU IMMUNOFOCO BIOTECHNOLOGY CO LTD [CN]

Provided is a use of immune cells in the preparation of a drug for preventing or treating a tumor; the immune cells are cells for adoptive immune cell therapy, which can target and kill EpCAM-expressing cells; and the tumor expresses EpCAM and is a metastatic tumor.

The novelty lies in the application of EpCAM-targeting immune cells (likely CAR-T or TCR-engineered cells) for metastatic tumor treatment, representing a specific antigen-targeting approach with potential clinical significance for solid tumors that typically express EpCAM.

patents.title: CHIMERIC ANTIGEN RECEPTOR CONTAINING CLDN18.2 SINGLE DOMAIN ANTIBODY AND APPLICATION THEREOF

The constructed chimeric antigen receptor is good in specificity, higher in safety in vivo use, and smaller in toxicity, and can provide a treatment solution for patients who suffer from advanced gastric cancer caused by high expression of a CLDN18.2 protein and currently undergo radiotherapy, chemotherapy, and surgery treatments.
patents.assignee: SHENZHEN IMMUNOFOCO BIOTECHNOLOGY CO LTD [CN]; SHENZHEN IMMUNOFOCO BIOTECHNOLOGY CO., LTD.
patents.novelty_summary: The patent describes a chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) utilizing a single domain antibody (sdAb) targeting CLDN18.2 instead of conventional full-length antibodies, enabling reduced CAR size and improved in vivo safety/specificity for gastric cancer treatment. The use of sdAb recognition units in CAR-T constructs represents a structural innovation that may enhance trafficking, penetration, and reduce off-target toxicity compared to conventional CAR-T designs.

patents.title: New Chimeric Receptor Composition, Recombinant Vector, Cell and Associated Use
patents.abstract: A novel chimeric receptor composition, a recombinant vector, a cell, and an application thereof. The novel chimeric receptor composition comprises a conventional chimeric antigen receptor (CAR), and an NKG2D chimeric receptor comprising full-length sequences or truncated fragments of NKG2D, DAP10, and/or DAP12, referred to as a SNR-armed CAR. The chimeric receptor composition enables a conventional CAR-T cell to express an NKG2D extracellular region and an intracellular signal region, expands a CAR-T antigen recognition spectrum, solves the tumor heterogeneity, achieves a lower level of factor release while enhancing the killing capability of CAR-T on tumor cells expressing target antigens, reduces the possibility of factor storm occurrence, and improves the CAR-T security.
patents.assignee: SUZHOU IMMUNOFOCO BIOTECHNOLOGY CO LTD [CN]; 苏州易慕峰生物科技有限公司
patents.novelty_summary: The patent presents a dual-receptor CAR-T construct combining conventional CAR with an NKG2D chimeric receptor (SNR-armed CAR) to expand antigen recognition spectrum and overcome tumor heterogeneity. This represents a clinically significant advancement for in vivo CAR-T therapy by reducing cytokine release while maintaining or enhancing anti-tumor efficacy and improving safety profile.

patents.assignee: SUZHOU IMMUNOFOCO BIOTECHNOLOGY CO LTD [CN]; Suzhou Immunofoco Biotechnology Co., Ltd.

The competitive significance lies in providing a humanized EpCAM-targeting CAR-T platform with reduced immunogenicity compared to murine antibodies, relevant to solid tumors expressing EpCAM (colorectal, gastric, ovarian cancers).

patents.title: METHODS AND COMPOSITIONS FOR TRANSDUCING AND EXPANDING LYMPHOCYTES AND REGULATING THE ACTIVITY THEREOF
patents.abstract: [0000]    The present disclosure provides methods for genetically modifying lymphocytes and methods for performing adoptive cellular therapy that include transducing T cells and/or NK cells. The methods can include inhibitory RNA molecule(s) and/or engineered signaling polypeptides that can include a lymphoproliferative element, and/or a chimeric antigen receptor (CAR), for example a microenvironment restricted biologic CAR (MRB-CAR). Additional elements of such engineered signaling polypeptides are provided herein, such as those that drive proliferation and regulatory elements therefor, as well as replication incompetent recombinant retroviral particles and packaging cell lines and methods of making the same. Numerous elements and methods for regulating transduced and/or genetically modified T cells and/or NK cells are provided, such as, for example, those including riboswitches, MRB-CARs, recognition domains, and/or pH-modulating agents.
patents.assignee: EXUMA BIOTECH CORP [US]; Exuma Biotech Corp.
patents.novelty_summary: The patent presents methods for transducing T cells and NK cells using engineered signaling polypeptides incorporating microenvironment-restricted biologic CARs (MRB-CARs) combined with inhibitory RNA molecules and lymphoproliferative elements. The competitive significance lies in the MRB-CAR technology that appears designed to restrict CAR activity to tumor microenvironments, potentially reducing off-target toxicity—a key challenge in in vivo CAR-T therapy.

patents.title: ANTI-IDIOTYPE COMPOSITIONS AND METHODS OF USE THEREOF
patents.abstract: The present disclosure provides methods and compositions that include a polynucleotide that includes nucleic acids that encode an anti-idiotype polypeptide, as well as polypeptides that are encoded by the same, and cells that include and express the polypeptide. Disclosed methods include methods that utilize the anti-idiotype polypeptides as safety switches when they are used in combination with antibodies, include approved biologic antibodies, that include the recognized idiotype. Certain embodiments include anti-idiotype polypeptides and nucleotides encoding the same, that include an internal domain. This internal domain in some embodiments has functional domains that can induce proliferation or cell death upon binding of the anti-idiotype polypeptide by its target antibody.
patents.assignee: EXUMA BIOTECH CORP [US]; Exuma Biotech Corp.
patents.novelty_summary: The patent discloses anti-idiotype polypeptides with internal functional domains that act as safety switches for antibody-based therapies, capable of inducing cell proliferation or death upon target binding. This represents a novel kill-switch architecture applicable to engineered cell therapies, offering a mechanism to control therapeutic cells expressing biologic antibodies through anti-idiotype recognition.

patents.title: VIRAL PARTICLES COMPRISING HYALURONIDASE BOUND TO A MEMBRANE
patents.abstract: Provided herein are methods, uses, compositions, and kits that include hyaluronidase polypeptides, including for example retroviral particles that include membrane bound hyaluronidase polypeptides, and novel, chimeric hyaluronidase polypeptides. Furthermore, provided herein are methods, uses, compositions, and kits that include hyaluronidase polypeptides, including for example retroviral particles that encode hyaluronidases and/or that include membrane bound hyaluronidases, which in some embodiments are novel, chimeric hyaluronidases provided herein. Accordingly, provided herein are replication incompetent recombinant retroviral particles (RIP), and methods using the same, that comprise a viral envelope, a nucleic acid encoding a packaging signal, Gag, and a membrane-bound hyaluronidase.

In some embodiments, modified lymphocytes are reintroduced into a subject subcutaneously. In some embodiments, polynucleotides that provide T cells the ability to regulate cell survival and proliferation in response to binding to a CAR, are provided.

Through verification, the recombinant virus can stably express CD55 and alphaPDL1 proteins, meanwhile, the genome stability is kept, and a research direction is provided for providing a novel biological preparation with high targeting property and high safety for treatment of malignant tumors such as colorectal cancer.

For in vivo CAR-T applications, this represents a complementary immunotherapy approach rather than direct CAR-T engineering, potentially useful in combination strategies to enhance endogenous T cell responses against cancer antigens.

patents.title: Methods for Production of Circular RNA, RNA Molecules and Their Uses
patents.abstract: A method for covalently joining linear RNA molecules end-to-end to extend their functionality. A cis-acting ligase ribozyme is used to generate circular RNA in vitro for ectopic protein expression. RNA circularization was confirmed by masking the 5' phosphate group, resisting exonuclease RNase R digestion, and sequencing the RT-PCR products of the joined region. Furthermore, one internal ribosome entry site rendered oRNA translation competent, but two IRES in cis, not tans, hampered the translation and an oRNA expressing ribonuclease Cas13 showed excellent potential against the corresponding RNA virus. A method for using oRNA is also provided.
patents.assignee: NATIONAL HEALTH RES INST [CN]; YUH CHIOU HWA [US]; NATIONAL HEALTH RESEARCH INSTITUTES
patents.novelty_summary: The patent describes a novel method for generating circular RNA (oRNA) using cis-acting ligase ribozymes to join linear RNA molecules, with demonstrated applications in ectopic protein expression and Cas13-based viral resistance. While the circular RNA platform itself has potential for improved mRNA stability and protein expression in gene therapy contexts, the patent does not specifically address CAR-T cell engineering or in vivo therapeutic applications, limiting its direct competitive significance for CAR-T therapy.
patents.title_original: MÉTHODES DE PRODUCTION D'ARN CIRCULAIRE, MOLÉCULES D'ARN ET LEURS UTILISATIONS

patents.title: Calcium phosphate transfection device
patents.abstract: The utility model discloses a calcium phosphate transfection device which particularly comprises a first liquid storage container, a second liquid storage container, a first quantitative container, a second quantitative container, a spinner bottle and a stirring device, the second liquid storage container is communicated with the second quantitative container through a guide pipe, and a one-way valve is arranged on the guide pipe to control flowing of liquid. According to the utility model, errors caused by manual experiment operation are reduced, the pollution risk in the operation process is reduced, the solution in the liquid storage container can be quantitatively dropped into the spinner bottle, the accuracy of the experiment is improved, and the experiment is simple and easy to operate.
patents.assignee: CARSGEN THERAPEUTICS SHANGHAI CO LTD; 科济生物医药（上海）有限公司

patents.title: Anti-Idiotype Compositions and Associated Methods of Use
patents.abstract: The present disclosure provides methods and compositions that include a polynucleotide that includes nucleic acids that encode an anti-idiotype polypeptide, as well as polypeptides that are encoded by the same, and cells that include and express the polypeptide. Disclosed methods include methods that utilize the anti-idiotype polypeptides as safety switches when they are used in combination with antibodies, include approved biologic antibodies, that include the recognized idiotype. Certain embodiments include anti-idiotype polypeptides and nucleotides encoding the same, that include an internal domain. This internal domain in some embodiments has functional domains that can induce proliferation or cell death upon binding of the anti-idiotype polypeptide by its target antibody.
patents.assignee: EXUMA BIOTECH CORP [US]; EXUMA BIOTECH CORP.
patents.novelty_summary: The patent discloses anti-idiotype polypeptides encoded by polynucleotides that function as conditional safety switches for antibody therapeutics, with internal domains capable of triggering proliferation or apoptosis upon target binding. This is significant for CAR-T because it represents a novel safety mechanism applicable to engineered T cells expressing antibody-like receptors, enabling inducible cell death or expansion in response to specific antigen recognition.
patents.title_original: COMPOSITIONS ANTI-IDIOTYPE ET PROCÉDÉS D'UTILISATION ASSOCIÉS

patents.title: Anti-Claudin 6 Antibody and Its Use
patents.abstract: An anti-CLDN6 antibody and an antigen-binding fragment thereof are disclosed in the present disclosure. In addition, a therapeutic use of the anti-CLDN6 antibody or the antigen-binding fragment thereof is disclosed in the present disclosure.
patents.assignee: ABL BIO INC [KR]; 에이비엘바이오 주식회사
patents.novelty_summary: The patent discloses novel anti-CLDN6 antibodies and their antigen-binding fragments as therapeutic agents. While claudin-6 is a recognized tumor-associated antigen, the specific antibody compositions and their therapeutic applications represent competitive value for targeting CLDN6-expressing cancers, including potential use in combination with CAR-T approaches or as standalone immunotherapy.

patents.title: Modified T7 RNA Polymerase
patents.abstract: The present disclosure addresses the problem of providing a modified T7 RNA polymerase.　The aforementioned problem is solved by providing a T7 RNA polymerase selected from any of the following (i) to (iii). (i) A T7 RNA polymerase having the amino acid sequence set forth in SEQ ID NO: 1, said amino acid sequence including at least the amino acid substitution indicated by (1): (1) a substitution in which an amino acid residue corresponding to the valine residue at position 114 in SEQ ID NO: 1 is substituted with an isoleucine residue, a threonine residue, an alanine residue, a cysteine residue, a glutamic acid residue, a lysine residue, a leucine residue, a methionine residue, an asparagine residue, a glutamine residue, an arginine residue, a serine residue, or a tryptophan residue; (ii) a T7 RNA polymerase having the amino acid sequence set forth in SEQ ID NO: 1, said amino acid sequence including at least the amino acid substitution indicated by (1), and furthermore including one or m
patents.assignee: TOSOH CORP [JP]; 東ソー株式会社
patents.novelty_summary: The patent discloses modified T7 RNA polymerase variants with amino acid substitutions at position 114, designed to improve polymerase properties. While T7 RNAP is a standard tool for in vitro transcription and IVT mRNA production used in some CAR-T manufacturing workflows, the specific novelty here (single position substitutions) has limited direct competitive significance for in vivo CAR-T therapies, though it may marginally improve IVT efficiency for synthetic mRNA delivery systems.
patents.title_original: ARN POLYMÉRASE T7 MODIFIÉE

patents.title: STABLE ANTIBODY FORMULATION COMPRISING FIANLIMAB
patents.abstract: The present invention provides stable pharmaceutical formulations comprising a human antibody that specifically binds to human lymphocyte activation gene-3 (LAG-3). In certain embodiments, the formulations contain, in addition to an anti-LAG-3 antibody, a buffer, an amino acid, a non-ionic surfactant, and a sugar. The pharmaceutical formulations of the present invention exhibit a substantial degree of antibody stability upon stress and storage.
patents.assignee: REGENERON PHARMA [US]; REGENERON PHARMACEUTICALS, INC.
patents.novelty_summary: The invention provides stable pharmaceutical formulations of fianlimab (anti-LAG-3 antibody) with optimized excipient composition (buffer, amino acid, non-ionic surfactant, sugar) that achieve enhanced stability under stress and storage conditions. This is competitively significant for in vivo CAR-T as LAG-3 checkpoint blockade is a validated approach to enhance CAR-T cell persistence and anti-tumor efficacy, and improved formulation stability reduces manufacturing costs and enables broader clinical deployment.

patents.title: BIO-PARTICLE ENCAPSULATED HYDROGEL USING AQUEOUS-TWO PHASE SYSTEM AND METHOD FOR PRODUCING SAME
patents.abstract: When a biological material sensitive to an external reaction is incorporated during hydrogel production, physical stimulation or chemical stimulation applied in conventional hydrogel production methods requires a sophisticated process and can affect the activity and structure of particles in the hydrogel. On the other hand, a hydrogel using an aqueous-two phase system and a method for producing same provided by the present invention can simultaneously achieve hydrogel formation and the encapsulation of desired nanoparticles in the hydrogel. The present invention has succeeded in simply concentrating desired nanoparticles in a hydrogel with a high yield. In addition, the present invention relates to a hydrogel using an aqueous-two phase system and a method for producing same, wherein concentration and hydrogel formation are simultaneously performed, and thus the time for producing the hydrogel is reduced and the cost is significantly reduced.
patents.assignee: PNASEER INC; PNASEER INC.
patents.novelty_summary: The patent describes an aqueous two-phase system (ATPS) for hydrogel production that enables gentle, simultaneous encapsulation of biological nanoparticles without harsh physical or chemical stimulation that typically damages sensitive biological materials. The competitive significance for cell therapy lies in potential applications for protecting and delivering therapeutic cells or biologics, though direct CAR-T applicability is not explicitly demonstrated in the available abstract.

patents.title: T7 RNA polymerase variant and use thereof
patents.abstract: Provided are a T7RNA polymerase variant and use thereof. The amino acid sequence of the T7RNA polymerase variant, relative to SEQ ID NO: 1, comprises at least one substitution or deletion selected from the following amino acid sites: R34, K172, Y178, R386, D388, Q435, N437, and D438. The variant, relative to a wild-type T7RNA polymerase, has improved catalytic activity, and can improve the capping rate of mRNA products during in vitro transcription. In addition, a method for preparing RNA using the variant is also provided. Using the method to prepare RNA molecules, more capped mRNAs can be obtained.
patents.assignee: NANJING VAZYME BIOTECH CO LTD [CN]; 南京诺唯赞生物科技股份有限公司
patents.novelty_summary: The patent discloses T7 RNA polymerase variants with specific amino acid substitutions/deletions that improve catalytic activity and mRNA capping rates during in vitro transcription. This is significant for gene therapy and CAR-T manufacturing as efficient, capped mRNA production is critical for mRNA-based therapeutics, including mRNA vaccines that may be combined with CAR-T approaches and in vitro transcribed mRNA used for transient transgene expression.
patents.title_original: VARIANT D'ARN POLYMÉRASE ET SON UTILISATION

patents.title: METHODS AND COMPOSITIONS FOR INDUCING HEMATOPOIETIC CELL DIFFERENTIATION
patents.abstract: [0000]    In various aspects, the invention provides culture platforms, cell media, and methods of differentiating pluripotent cells into hematopoietic cells. In certain aspects, the invention further provides pluripotent stem cell-derived hematopoietic cells generated using the culture media and methods disclosed herein. The pluripotent stem cell-derived definitive HE cells produced by methods provided herein are capable of differentiating into hematopoietic lineage cells comprising T cell progenitors and T cells, in addition to NK cell progenitors, NK cells, NKT cells, or B cells.
patents.assignee: FATE THERAPEUTICS INC [US]; FATE THERAPEUTICS, INC.
patents.novelty_summary: The patent discloses novel culture platforms and media formulations for efficiently differentiating pluripotent stem cells into hematopoietic cells, particularly those capable of generating T cell progenitors and mature T cells. This is significant for CAR-T therapy as it provides an alternative scalable source of T cells derived from pluripotent stem cells rather than primary patient isolation, potentially enabling off-the-shelf, allogeneic CAR-T manufacturing.

patents.title: BISPECIFIC ANTIBODIES AGAINST CEACAM5 AND CD3
patents.abstract: The present invention relates to bispecific antibodies which bind to human carcinoembryonic antigen CEACAM5 (CEA) and human CD3ε. In addition, the present invention relates to polynucleotides encoding such bispecific antibodies and vectors and host cells comprising such polynucleotides. The invention further relates to methods for selecting and producing such antibodies and to methods of using such antibodies in the treatment of diseases.
patents.assignee: LAMKAP BIO ALPHA AG [CH]; LamKap Bio Alpha AG
patents.novelty_summary: Bispecific antibodies that simultaneously engage CEACAM5 on tumor cells and CD3ε on T cells to redirect T cell cytotoxicity toward CEA-expressing cancers. This represents a T cell-engaging bispecific antibody (BiTE) approach competing with CAR-T by offering an off-the-shelf, allogeneic therapeutic without genetic engineering of patient T cells, potentially reducing manufacturing complexity and cost while targeting CEA+ solid tumors.

patents.title: METHODS OF PREPARING MITOCHONDRIA REPLACED CELLS WITH IMPROVED MITOCHONDRIAL FUNCTION
patents.abstract: [0000]    The present invention provides methods and compositions for generation of mitochondria replaced cells (MirC), and therapeutic methods for using such compositions for treating a subject having an age-related disease or syndrome, mitochondrial disease or disorder, or otherwise in need of mitochondrial replacement. Also provided are methods and compositions for producing a recipient cell having a mitochondrial disease or disorder, as well as methods and compositions for producing or enhancing production of an inducible pluripotent stem cell (iPSC). In addition, methods and compositions to enhance mitochondrial transfer are also included.
patents.assignee: IMEL BIOTHERAPEUTICS INC [US]; Imel Biotherapeutics, Inc.
patents.novelty_summary: The patent describes methods for generating mitochondria-replaced cells (MirC) with improved mitochondrial function and their therapeutic application in treating age-related diseases, mitochondrial disorders, and related conditions. While the core technology addresses mitochondrial replacement rather than CAR-T engineering directly, it presents potential utility as an enabling platform for enhancing T cell function by correcting mitochondrial dysfunction—a known limitation in CAR-T cell persistence and anti-tumor efficacy.

patents.title: Method for assessing the validity of a cell therapy product
patents.abstract: The present invention provides a method for evaluating effectiveness of a cell therapeutic agent. When using TGF-β and/or TSP-1 expression level(s) in: (a) a first population of transformed mammalian cells with TGF-β; and (b) a second population of untransformed mammalian cells with the same gene, respectively, as a criterion for determining effectiveness of a cell therapeutic agent, and whether or not expression thereof, it is possible to definitely determine the therapeutic efficacy of each cell therapeutic agent prior to initiation of the treatment. In addition, since use of a cell therapeutic agent without therapeutic effects is avoided, undesired procedures and side effects may not be entailed.
patents.assignee: KOLON LIFE SCIENCE INC [KR]; KOLON TISSUEGENE INC [US]; Kolon Life Science, Inc.
patents.novelty_summary: The invention describes a method for evaluating the therapeutic efficacy of cell therapeutic agents by measuring TGF-β and/or TSP-1 expression levels in transformed versus untransformed mammalian cells as predictive biomarkers prior to treatment initiation. This quality control approach is significant for cell therapy manufacturing as it enables pre-clinical efficacy assessment and reduces risk of administering ineffective products, though the clinical application scope and specificity to CAR-T versus other cell therapies is unclear from the abstract.
patents.title_original: VERFAHREN ZUR BEURTEILUNG DER GÜLTIGKEIT EINES ZELLTHERAPIEPRODUKTS

patents.title: BISPECIFIC T CELL ACTIVATING ANTIGEN BINDING MOLECULES
patents.abstract: The present invention generally relates to novel bispecific antigen binding molecules for T cell activation and re-direction to specific target cells. In addition, the present invention relates to polynucleotides encoding such bispecific antigen binding molecules, and vectors and host cells comprising such polynucleotides. The invention further relates to methods for producing the bispecific antigen binding molecules of the invention, and to methods of using these bispecific antigen binding molecules in the treatment of disease.
patents.assignee: ROCHE GLYCART AG [CH]; Roche Glycart AG
patents.novelty_summary: The patent discloses novel bispecific antigen binding molecules that simultaneously engage T cell activation receptors and target cell antigens, enabling T cell redirection to specific disease targets without genetic modification. This represents a significant competitive alternative to CAR-T therapy, offering off-the-shelf bispecific T cell engagers (BiTEs) with potentially faster manufacturing timelines and reduced manufacturing complexity compared to autologous CAR-T cell engineering.

patents.title: R2 RETROTRANSPOSONS FOR GENE WRITING
patents.assignee: UNIV TOKYO [JP]; TYPEWRITER THERAPEUTICS INC [US]; THE UNIVERSITY OF TOKYO
patents.novelty_summary: The patent presents R2 retrotransposons as novel genetic tools for precise DNA insertion and gene writing applications. This technology could be significant for CAR-T engineering by enabling more controlled genomic integration of CAR constructs with reduced off-target effects compared to traditional integrase-based systems, potentially improving safety and efficacy profiles.

patents.title: System and method for culturing NK cells and their use
patents.abstract: The present invention relates to the field of immune cell therapy, and specifically relates to a method for expanding NK cells and use thereof. The method comprises using OK-432 in combination with irradiated feeder cells, such as K562 cells, to expand and culture NK cells in vitro.
patents.assignee: SHENZHEN GENOCURY BIOTECH CO LTD [CN]; 深圳市济因生物科技有限公司
patents.novelty_summary: The invention describes a novel in vitro NK cell expansion method combining OK-432 (Picibanil) with irradiated K562 feeder cells, offering an alternative approach to CAR-T-like immunotherapy. While NK cell engineering represents an adjacent therapeutic modality to CAR-T, this composition-based culture method may have competitive implications for off-the-shelf cellular immunotherapy products due to NK cells' reduced immunogenicity and lack of GvHD liability.

patents.title: LIPID NANOPARTICLES FOR BIOPRODUCTION
patents.abstract: A nonviral gene therapy delivers DNA that allows cells to produce proteins such as their own growth factors in culture media. Lipid nanoparticles provide an effective delivery mechanism into a target cell. By encapsulating plasmid DNA encoding the growth factors with inducible promoters into lipid nanoparticles (LNPs), target cells create their own growth factors reducing a need for expensive growth factors from external sources. DNA expression lasts for several days reducing the amount of reagent needed. The plasmid DNA is more stable than mRNA and proteins, therefore reducing logistical challenges.
patents.assignee: WORCESTER POLYTECHNIC INST [US]; Worcester Polytechnic Institute
patents.novelty_summary: The patent describes LNP-mediated delivery of plasmid DNA with inducible promoters enabling in situ production of growth factors (e.g., cytokines) in cultured cells, reducing dependency on exogenous supplementation. This approach leverages plasmid DNA stability advantages over mRNA while enabling transient protein expression for cost reduction in cell manufacturing—potentially applicable to reducing GMP costs in CAR-T cell expansion.

patents.title: Single-Domain Antibody Targeting Nectin-4, Chimeric Antigen Receptor, and Associated Uses
patents.abstract: The present invention relates to the field of biomedicine, and in particular to a Nectin-4-targeting single-domain antibody, a chimeric antigen receptor, and a use thereof. The provided anti-Nectin-4 single-domain antibody has the advantages of low molecular weight, high solubility, high stability, low immunogenicity, and high tissue permeability, and requires no additional folding and assembly steps or linker optimization and modification, so that said antibody becomes a promising alternative to antibodies having a large molecular weight, such as monoclonal antibodies and scFv single-chain antibodies.
patents.assignee: SHENZHEN GENOCURY BIOTECH CO LTD [CN]; 深圳市济因生物科技有限公司
patents.novelty_summary: The invention provides a Nectin-4-targeting single-domain antibody with improved biophysical properties (low molecular weight, high solubility, stability, and tissue permeability) integrated into a chimeric antigen receptor format. This represents a competitive advantage for in vivo CAR-T applications by potentially enabling superior tumor penetration and reduced immunogenicity compared to conventional scFv-based CAR constructs, while eliminating the need for linker optimization.

patents.title: Gene editing tools and compositions for cell engineering
patents.abstract: The present invention relates to a composition comprising a transposase, optionally a RNA-guided nuclease, and a supercoiled circular dsDNA molecule comprising a transgene flanked by ITRs, in particular for its use as a gene editing tool.
patents.assignee: INTEGRA THERAPEUTICS [ES]; INTEGRA THERAPEUTICS
patents.novelty_summary: The patent discloses a composition combining transposase, optional RNA-guided nuclease, and supercoiled circular dsDNA with transgene flanked by ITRs as an integrated gene editing tool. This combination approach for non-viral gene delivery and cell engineering offers potential advantages in CAR-T manufacturing by enabling efficient integration of CAR constructs without viral vectors, potentially improving scalability and reducing manufacturing complexity.
