patents.title: Chimeric Antigen Receptors Targeting CD19
patents.abstract: Provided herein are RNA sequences encoding a chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) comprising a CD19 antigen binding molecule, along with related compositions and methods. In some embodiments, circular RNAs encoding the CD19 binding molecule or CD19 CAR, along with related compositions, methods, and precursors, are described herein. In some embodiments, these compositions comprise a transfer vehicle, e.g., comprising an ionizable lipid described herein.
patents.assignee: ORNA THERAPEUTICS INC [US]; RENAGADE THERAPEUTICS MAN INC [US]; Orna Therapeutics, Inc.
patents.novelty_summary: The patent describes circular RNA (circRNA) encoding CD19-targeting CAR constructs delivered via ionizable lipid-based transfer vehicles, representing a novel delivery modality alternative to viral vectors and linear mRNA for in vivo CAR-T cell engineering. The use of circular RNA architecture offers potential advantages in stability, reduced innate immune activation, and sustained protein expression, with significant competitive implications for non-viral CAR-T cell manufacturing and therapeutic efficacy.

patents.title: Method for producing carrier particles for cultivating biological cells and their application for cultivating biological cells
patents.abstract: The invention relates to a method for producing carrier particles for cultivating biological cells, particularly dried hydrogel particles, and to applications and bioreactors comprising such carrier particles. The invention can be used in the cultivation of biological cells, in particular in the cultivation (expansion) of multipotent and pluripotent stem cells or differentiated cells, for example for tissue engineering. The invention further relates to a freeze dryer designed to carry out the method. The method for producing carrier particles for cultivating biological cells comprises the steps of: providing (S10) an aqueous suspension of hydrogel beads, freeze-drying (S30) the hydrogel beads such that dried hydrogel particles are formed, storing (S40) the freeze-dried hydrogel particles, and subsequently rehydrating (S50) the hydrogel particles by adding an aqueous cultivation medium for cultivating biological cells. The method is characterised in that the freeze-drying (S30) of the h
patents.assignee: FRAUNHOFER GES ZUR FOERDERUNG DER ANGEWANDTEN FORSCHUNG E V [DE]; UNIV DES SAARLANDES KOERPERSCHAFT DES OEFFENTLICHEN RECHTS [DE]; FRAUNHOFER-GESELLSCHAFT ZUR FÖRDERUNG DER ANGEWANDTEN FORSCHUNG E. V.
patents.novelty_summary: The invention describes a method for producing freeze-dried hydrogel particles as carrier substrates for cell cultivation, with potential applications in stem cell expansion and tissue engineering. The novelty lies in the specific freeze-drying process for hydrogel bead preservation and their storage stability, which could provide cost-effective and scalable alternatives to traditional culture systems for cell expansion.
patents.title_original: VERFAHREN ZUR HERSTELLUNG VON TRÄGERPARTIKELN FÜR DIE KULTIVIERUNG BIOLOGISCHER ZELLEN UND DEREN ANWENDUNG FÜR DIE KULTIVIERUNG BIOLOGISCHER ZELLEN

patents.title: Hydrogel-based vehicle for the release of a biologic
patents.abstract: A hydrogel-based biological delivery vehicle used to effectively deliver drug and biological material to tissue or organ sites. More specifically, a hydrogel binding matrix having a biopolymer backbone containing carboxyl groups. Tyramine may be substituted for at least a portion of the carboxyl groups, so that, when hydrogen peroxide is added, it causes creation of covalent bonds between tyramine molecules and cross-links the hydrogel binding matrix, thereby enabling the hydrogel binding matrix to transition from liquid to gel state. The hydrogel binding matrix, in its liquid form, is capable of encapsulating drug reservoirs to create a homogenous liquid with evenly distributed particles containing drugs or target molecules. As the hydrogel binding matrix solidifies into a gel state, the newly created cross-links do not disrupt or react with the drugs or target molecules contained within the drug reservoirs. This hydrogel-based biological delivery vehicle can be used in several medica
patents.assignee: INSITU BIOLOGICS INC [US]; Insitu Biologics, Inc.
patents.novelty_summary: The patent describes a tyramine-substituted hydrogel with carboxyl groups that cross-links via hydrogen peroxide to transition from liquid to gel state while encapsulating biologics. This represents a novel delivery platform technology potentially applicable to cell and gene therapies, offering controlled spatial and temporal release of therapeutic agents at tissue sites.
patents.title_original: HYDROGELBASIERTES VEHIKEL ZUR FREISETZUNG EINES BIOLOGIKUMS

patents.title: LIPID NANOPARTICLES FOR DELIVERY OF THERAPEUTIC PAYLOADS TO CELLS
patents.abstract: The disclosure provides ionizable lipids for constructing lipid nanoparticles. The disclosure further provides conjugates comprising a targeting moiety and a lipid nanoparticle (LNP) encapsulating a therapeutic agent (e.g., payload) for delivery to immune cells, hematopoietic stem cells (HSCs), or liver cells. The conjugates can be delivered to cells ex vivo or formulated in a pharmaceutical composition to be directly administered to a subject in need thereof (e.g., via in vivo administration).
patents.assignee: TESSERA THERAPEUTICS INC; TESSERA THERAPEUTICS, INC.
patents.novelty_summary: The patent discloses ionizable lipids and LNP conjugates with targeting moieties for selective delivery to immune cells and HSCs, enabling both ex vivo and in vivo therapeutic payload delivery. This is significant for in vivo CAR-T as it addresses the key challenge of achieving targeted lymphocyte transduction without systemic toxicity, potentially enabling direct in vivo CAR-T cell engineering.

patents.title: LIPID NANOPARTICLES FOR DELIVERY OF THERAPEUTIC PAYLOADS TO CELLS
patents.assignee: TESSERA THERAPEUTICS INC; TESSERA THERAPEUTICS, INC.
patents.novelty_summary: The patent claims lipid nanoparticle (LNP) compositions designed for therapeutic payload delivery to cells. LNPs represent a critical enabling technology for non-viral delivery of genetic material (mRNA, DNA) to T cells and other cell types, offering potential advantages over viral vectors in manufacturing scalability and immunogenicity profiles for in vivo CAR-T and other cell therapy applications.

patents.title: RNA FOR IN VIVO TRANSFECTION WITH INCREASED EXPRESSION
patents.abstract: This disclosure provides improved RNA molecules, including mRNA molecules that can be produced by in vitro transcription and are suitable for in vivo transfection using an appropriate delivery vehicle, such as a lipid nanoparticle (LNP) or targeted lipid nanoparticle (tLNP). The improved RNA include particular combinations of 5' untranslated region (UTR) and 3' UTR, particular 3' UTRs, or particular open reading frame sequences. Also provided herein are compositions of the LNP, or tLNP with an antibody as a targeting moiety, such as anti-CD8 antibodies that are used as targeting moiety.
patents.assignee: CAPSTAN THERAPEUTICS INC; CAPSTAN THERAPEUTICS, INC.
patents.novelty_summary: The patent discloses optimized mRNA molecules with specific combinations of 5' and 3' UTRs and ORF sequences designed for enhanced in vivo expression via LNP/tLNP delivery. For in vivo CAR-T applications, the targeted LNP formulation with anti-CD8 antibodies as targeting moieties represents a significant advance in directing mRNA-based CAR-T cell engineering to CD8+ T cells in vivo, potentially enabling direct CAR engineering without ex vivo cell manipulation.

patents.title: Lachnospiraceae bacterium ND2006 Cas12a mutant genes and polypeptides encoded by same
patents.abstract: 19861146_1 (GHMatters) P116964.AU This invention pertains to mutant Lachnospiraceae bacterium ND2006 (Lb) Cas12a nucleic acids and proteins for use in CRISPR/Cas12a endonuclease systems, and their methods of use. In particular, the invention pertains to an isolated mutant LbCas12a protein, wherein the isolated mutant LbCas12a protein is active in a CRISPR/Cas12a endonuclease system. The invention also includes isolated nucleic acids encoding mutant LbCas12a proteins, ribonucleoprotein complexes and CRISPR/Cas12a endonuclease systems having mutant LbCas12a proteins. pr p r
patents.assignee: INTEGRATED DNA TECHNOLOGIES INC; Integrated DNA Technologies, Inc.
patents.novelty_summary: The invention discloses mutant Lachnospiraceae bacterium ND2006 Cas12a proteins and encoding nucleic acids with improved activity in CRISPR/Cas12a endonuclease systems. While Cas12a is a known gene-editing tool, engineered mutants with enhanced activity could improve on-target editing efficiency and reduce off-target effects in therapeutic applications, including potential ex vivo CAR-T cell engineering.

patents.title: ANTIBODIES BINDING TO CD3
patents.abstract: The present invention generally relates to antibodies that bind to CD3, including multispecific antibodies e.g. for activating T cells. In addition, the present invention relates to polynucleotides encoding such antibodies, and vectors and host cells comprising such polynucleotides. The invention further relates to methods for producing the antibodies, and to methods of using them in the treatment of disease.
patents.assignee: HOFFMANN LA ROCHE INC [US]; Hoffmann-La Roche Inc.
patents.novelty_summary: The patent covers multispecific antibodies binding to CD3 with T cell activation capabilities, along with encoding polynucleotides, vectors, and host cells for production. This is significant for in vivo CAR-T as CD3-engaging bispecific/multispecific antibodies represent an alternative or complementary approach to direct CAR-T engineering, enabling T cell recruitment and activation without genetic modification.

patents.title: Methods and Compositions for Prophylactic Treatment to Prevent CRS
patents.abstract: Provided herein are the methods of using an anti-inflammatory agent for prophylactic therapy to prevent or alleviate CRS and/or NE associated with therapeutic interventions, such as the administration of a nucleic acid encoding a CAR.
patents.assignee: SHENZHEN GENOCURY BIOTECH CO LTD [CN]; SHENZHEN GENOCURY BIOTECH CO., LTD
patents.novelty_summary: The patent addresses prophylactic use of anti-inflammatory agents to prevent cytokine release syndrome (CRS) and neurotoxicity (NE) associated with CAR-T cell therapy. This is clinically significant as CRS/NE remain major safety liabilities limiting CAR-T adoption; pre-emptive anti-inflammatory strategies could improve tolerability and expand treatment populations.
patents.title_original: PROCÉDÉS ET COMPOSITIONS DE TRAITEMENT PROPHYLACTIQUE POUR PRÉVENIR UN CRS

patents.title: Use of TERT gene in detection of residual iPSCs
patents.abstract: Disclosed in the present invention is the use of a TERT gene in the detection of residual iPSCs, which can effectively detect the presence of residual iPSCs in differentiated cells derived from hiPSCs, such as iNK cells.
patents.assignee: SHENZHEN GENOCURY BIOTECH CO LTD [CN]; 深圳市济因生物科技有限公司
patents.novelty_summary: The invention uses TERT gene expression as a biomarker to detect residual undifferentiated iPSCs in differentiated cell products, particularly iNK cells derived from hiPSCs. This addresses a critical quality control challenge in cell therapy manufacturing where residual pluripotent cells pose tumorigenicity risks, relevant to ensuring safety of engineered cell therapies including CAR-T products derived from iPSC platforms.
patents.title_original: UTILISATION DU GÈNE TERT DANS LA DÉTECTION DES IPSC RÉSIDUELLES

patents.title: Humanized Anti-MSLN Antibody and Use Thereof
patents.abstract: The present invention provides a humanized anti-MSLN antibody and a use thereof. The humanized MSLN antibody of the present invention is modified to improve affinity, and the affinity thereof for binding to a human MSLN antigen is equal to or better than that of a commercially available humanized anti-MSLN antibody.
patents.assignee: SHENZHEN GENOCURY BIOTECH CO LTD [CN]; 深圳市济因生物科技有限公司
patents.novelty_summary: This patent describes a humanized anti-MSLN antibody with improved binding affinity to human MSLN antigen compared to commercially available humanized anti-MSLN antibodies. While MSLN is a relevant tumor-associated antigen for CAR-T therapy, the patent focuses on antibody composition rather than CAR-T cell engineering or in vivo therapeutic application, limiting its direct competitive significance for CAR-T.
patents.title_original: ANTICORPS ANTI-MSLN HUMANISÉ ET UTILISATION DE CELUI-CI

patents.title: Humanized anti-CD3 antibodies and their uses
patents.abstract: Provided are humanized framework region templates for the development of humanized antibodies. Further provided are the humanized anti-CD3ε antibodies. The humanized anti-CD3ε antibodies described herein are useful in methods for modulating an immune response.
patents.assignee: SHENZHEN GENOCURY BIOTECH CO LTD [CN]; SHENZHEN GENOCURY BIOTECH CO., LTD
patents.novelty_summary: The patent describes humanized anti-CD3ε antibodies with novel humanized framework region templates designed to reduce immunogenicity while maintaining binding affinity. These antibodies are significant for CAR-T engineering as anti-CD3 antibodies are critical tools for T cell activation, expansion, and manufacturing in ex vivo CAR-T production workflows.
patents.title_original: ANTICORPS ANTI-CD3 HUMANISÉS ET LEURS UTILISATIONS

patents.title: Novel ionizable lipid, preparation method therefor, and use thereof
patents.abstract: Provided in the present invention are a novel ionizable lipid, a preparation method therefor, and the use thereof. The structural formula of the novel ionizable lipid is as shown in formula (I). An ionizable lipid compound of the present invention contains structures of urea and a bioisostere thereof. By virtue of hydrogen bonds which squaramide, urea, and thiourea structures form with nucleic acid, the encapsulation effect of the ionizable lipid is enhanced and the immunogenicity of the ionizable lipid is reduced. Nanoparticles prepared using the ionizable lipid of the present invention have a high encapsulation efficiency, a low PDI, and a broadly adaptable and stable process.
patents.assignee: SHENZHEN MAGICRNA BIOTECHNOLOGY CO LTD [CN]; 深圳虹信生物科技有限公司
patents.novelty_summary: The patent discloses a novel ionizable lipid containing urea and bioisosteric structures (squaramide, thiourea) that enhance hydrogen bonding with nucleic acids, improving encapsulation efficiency and reducing immunogenicity. This is competitive for in vivo CAR-T delivery as ionizable lipids are critical for mRNA-LNP formulations used to deliver CAR-T constructs, and reduced immunogenicity with improved encapsulation directly enhances therapeutic efficacy and safety.
patents.title_original: NOUVEAU LIPIDE IONISABLE, SON PROCÉDÉ DE PRÉPARATION ET SON UTILISATION

patents.title: Use of JAK inhibitors to enhance the potency of immunotherapy in cancer treatment
patents.abstract: Immunotherapy leverages the body's immune system to target cancer cells, but some tumors resist this treatment due to low infiltration of T CD8+ cells and high infiltration of regulatory T cells in the tumor microenvironment. The inventors showed that a JAK inhibitor (i.e. ruxolitinib) reshapes the tumor immune microenvironment resulting in T regulatory cells reduction and T CD8+ cells increase. Ruxolitinib-mediated immune microenvironment effects create new therapeutic opportunities by enhancing anti-PD1 treatment efficacy in cSCC and melanoma and other immunotherapy resistant cancer types such as pancreatic cancer and acute myeloid leukemia (AML). Cell-based immunotherapy response is also improved in AML. Accordingly, the present invention relates to the use of JAK inhibitors for enhancing the potency of immunotherapy.
patents.assignee: INSTITUT NATIONAL DE LA SANTE ET DE LA RECH MEDICALE [FR]; ASSIST PUBLIQUE HOPITAUX DE PARIS APHP [FR]; CENTRE NATIONAL DE LA RECHERCHE SCIENT [FR]
patents.novelty_summary: The patent describes using JAK inhibitors (specifically ruxolitinib) to reshape the tumor microenvironment by reducing regulatory T cells and increasing CD8+ T cell infiltration, thereby enhancing the efficacy of checkpoint inhibitor immunotherapy and cell-based immunotherapy in immunotherapy-resistant cancers. This approach offers significant competitive value for improving CAR-T cell infiltration and functionality in solid tumors and hematologic malignancies where low T cell infiltration is a limiting factor.
patents.title_original: UTILISATION D'INHIBITEURS DE JAK POUR AMÉLIORER LA PUISSANCE DE L'IMMUNOTHÉRAPIE DANS LE TRAITEMENT DU CANCER

patents.title: Methods of Detection of B Cell Depletion and Treatment of B Cell-Mediated Diseases
patents.abstract: The present disclosure provides methods of treating a subject having or suspected of having a B cell malignancy or a B cell mediated disorder by administering hypoimmune allogenic CD19-directed CAR T cells. Also disclosed are pharmaceutical compositions comprising hypoimmune allogenic CD19-directed CAR T cells, for use in treating a subject having or suspected of having a B cell malignancy or a B cell mediated disorder.
patents.assignee: SANA BIOTECHNOLOGY INC [US]; SANA BIOTECHNOLOGY, INC.
patents.novelty_summary: The patent discloses hypoimmune allogeneic CD19-directed CAR T cells for treating B cell malignancies and B cell-mediated disorders. The competitive significance lies in the use of allogeneic (off-the-shelf) hypoimmune CAR T cells rather than autologous cells, potentially enabling faster manufacturing, reduced immunogenicity, and broader accessibility for in vivo CAR-T therapy.
patents.title_original: MÉTHODES DE DÉTECTION DE LA DÉPLÉTION DES LYMPHOCYTES B ET DE TRAITEMENT DE MALADIES MÉDIÉES PAR LES LYMPHOCYTES B

patents.title: Engineered retrotransposable element proteins for gene delivery and insertion
patents.assignee: AVERNA THERAPEUTICS LTD [IL]; AVERNA THERAPEUTICS LTD
patents.novelty_summary: The patent describes engineered retrotransposable element proteins optimized for gene delivery and genomic insertion, offering a novel non-viral delivery platform distinct from viral vectors and conventional transposons. This technology is relevant to CAR-T engineering as it provides an alternative mechanism for stable transgene integration into T cells, potentially improving efficiency and safety compared to existing integration methods.

patents.title: Viral vectors and packaging cell lines
patents.assignee: UMOJA BIOPHARMA INC [US]; UMOJA BIOPHARMA INC.

patents.title: Constrained ionizable cationic lipids and lipid nanoparticles
patents.assignee: CAPSTAN THERAPEUTICS INC [US]; KARMALI PRIYA PRAKASH [US]; TANIS STEVEN [US]
patents.novelty_summary: The patent describes novel constrained ionizable cationic lipids with structural constraints designed to improve lipid nanoparticle (LNP) formulation properties. These lipids are relevant to gene therapy delivery as optimized LNPs can enhance mRNA delivery efficiency and cellular uptake, which is significant for CAR-T manufacturing and in vivo therapeutic applications requiring improved transfection.

patents.title: CHIMERIC ANTIGEN RECEPTOR TARGETING CD19
patents.abstract: Provided herein are RNA sequences encoding a chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) comprising a CD19 antigen binding molecule, along with related compositions and methods. In some embodiments, circular RNAs encoding the CD19 binding molecule or CD19 CAR, along with related compositions, methods, and precursors, are described herein. In some embodiments, these compositions comprise a transfer vehicle, e.g., comprising an ionizable lipid described herein.
patents.assignee: ORNA THERAPEUTICS INC [US]; RENAGADE THERAPEUTICS MAN INC [US]; ORNA THERAPEUTICS, INC.
patents.novelty_summary: The patent discloses circular RNA (circRNA) encoding CD19-targeting CAR with ionizable lipid-based delivery vehicles, representing a non-viral delivery approach distinct from viral vectors or linear RNA modalities. This is competitively significant for in vivo CAR-T as circRNA offers improved stability, reduced immunogenicity, and self-amplifying potential compared to conventional mRNA, while ionizable lipids enable efficient lymphocyte transfection without viral integration risk.
patents.title_original: RÉCEPTEUR ANTIGÉNIQUE CHIMÉRIQUE CIBLANT CD19

patents.title: Therapeutic Use of Protein Heterodimer
patents.abstract: [0001]    Use of a protein heterodimer in the preparation of a drug, which drug is used for preventing and/or treating malignant effusion. The protein heterodimer contains a first member and a second member different from the first member, wherein the first member contains a light chain and a heavy chain, the heavy chain contains a first Fc region, and the light chain is complexed with the heavy chain to form a targeting moiety that exhibits binding specificity for a tumor antigen; and the second member contains a polypeptide containing an immunomodulator fused to a second Fc region. The first member and the second member are associated by means of the complexing of the first Fc region with the second Fc region so as to form the heterodimer. In addition, the first Fc region contains a first modification and/or the second Fc region contains a second modification, and these modifications can more effectively promote heterodimerization between the first member and the second member.
patents.assignee: SHIHUIDA PHARMACEUTICAL GROUP JILIN CO LTD [CN]; Shihuida Pharmaceutical Group (Jilin) Co., Ltd.
patents.novelty_summary: The patent discloses a protein heterodimer comprising a targeting moiety (antibody-like structure with tumor antigen specificity) fused to an Fc region, complexed with an immunomodulator-Fc fusion protein. The innovation lies in the specific Fc region pairing strategy to create a bispecific or multispecific therapeutic for malignant effusion treatment, potentially offering improved tumor targeting and immune activation compared to monoclonal antibodies alone.
patents.title_original: THERAPEUTISCHE VERWENDUNG VON PROTEIN-HETERODIMER

patents.title: Hyperactive Transposons and Transposases
patents.abstract: [0001]    The present invention relates to a polypeptide comprising a piggyBac transposase or a fragment or a derivative thereof having transposase function comprising at least one amino acid substitution. Further, the present invention relates to a transposable element comprising a piggyBac or piggyBac-like left repeat sequence and left internal repeat sequence, wherein the left internal repeat sequence comprises at least one nucleotide modification. Furthermore, the present invention relates to a kit comprising the above transposase and/or transposable element. In addition, the present invention relates to a targeting system comprising the above transposase and/or transposable element.
patents.assignee: PROBIOGEN AG [DE]; ProBioGen AG
patents.novelty_summary: The patent discloses hyperactive piggyBac transposase variants with amino acid substitutions and modified transposable elements with nucleotide modifications in repeat sequences, designed to enhance transposition efficiency. This is significant for in vivo CAR-T applications as improved transposases enable more efficient non-viral genomic integration of CAR constructs, potentially reducing off-target effects and improving therapeutic efficacy compared to wild-type transposition systems.
patents.title_original: HYPERAKTIVE TRANSPOSONS UND TRANSPOSASEN

patents.title: Lipid nanoparticles for delivery of therapeutic payloads to cells
patents.assignee: TESSERA THERAPEUTICS INC [US]; WANG ZHAN [US]; ZHANG RUI [US]
patents.novelty_summary: The patent describes lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) engineered for targeted delivery of therapeutic payloads to cells, representing a delivery vehicle innovation relevant to gene therapy and cell engineering applications. The competitive significance lies in optimizing LNP formulations for improved cellular uptake and therapeutic efficacy, which is critical for in vivo CAR-T cell manufacturing and ex vivo T cell engineering where genetic cargo delivery efficiency directly impacts therapeutic potency.

patents.title: ANTIBODIES BINDING TO CEACAM5
patents.abstract: The present invention generally relates to antibodies that bind to CEACAM5. In addition, the present invention relates to polynucleotides encoding such antibodies, and vectors and host cells comprising such polynucleotides. The invention further relates to methods for producing the antibodies, and to methods of using them in the treatment of disease.
patents.assignee: F HOFFMANN LA ROCHE AG; F. HOFFMANN-LA ROCHE AG
patents.novelty_summary: The patent discloses novel antibodies targeting CEACAM5 with associated polynucleotides, vectors, and host cell systems for antibody production. While CEACAM5 is a known tumor-associated antigen, the specific novelty lies in the antibody compositions and their therapeutic application; competitive significance for in vivo CAR-T is moderate—CEACAM5 targeting could support dual-specificity or tandem CAR designs, but the patent itself focuses on antibody therapeutics rather than CAR-T engineering.

patents.title: BISPECIFIC T CELL ACTIVATING ANTIGEN BINDING MOLECULES
patents.abstract: The present invention generally relates to novel bispecific antigen binding molecules for T cell activation and re-direction to specific target cells. In addition, the present invention relates to polynucleotides encoding such bispecific antigen binding molecules, and vectors and host cells comprising such polynucleotides. The invention further relates to methods for producing the bispecific antigen binding molecules of the invention, and to methods of using these bispecific antigen binding molecules in the treatment of disease.
patents.assignee: ROCHE GLYCART AG [CH]; Roche Glycart AG
patents.novelty_summary: The patent claims bispecific antigen binding molecules that simultaneously engage T cell activation receptors and target cell antigens, enabling T cell redirection without genetic modification. This represents a significant competitive advantage for in vivo CAR-T applications as it offers an off-the-shelf, non-genetically modified alternative to CAR-T cell therapy, potentially addressing manufacturing complexity, cost, and scalability limitations inherent to autologous CAR-T approaches.

patents.title: CIRCULAR RNA COMPOSITIONS
patents.abstract: Provided herein are circular RNA constructs comprising an IRES, and at least one expression sequence encoding binding molecule, compositions thereof, and methods of treating autoimmune disease. In particular, circular RNA comprising an IRES and a CD19 binder or a BCMA binder are provided, optionally formulated with a delivery vehicle. Precursor polynucleotides comprising an IRES, and at least one expression sequence encoding a CAR construct are also described herein.
patents.assignee: ORNA THERAPEUTICS INC; ORNA THERAPEUTICS, INC.
patents.novelty_summary: The patent discloses circular RNA constructs with IRES elements for expressing CAR molecules (CD19 or BCMA-targeting binders) and precursor polynucleotides encoding full CAR constructs. The competitive significance lies in using self-replicating circular RNA as an alternative to linear mRNA for CAR-T cell engineering, potentially offering improved expression kinetics, reduced immunogenicity, and enhanced durability compared to conventional viral vectors or transient mRNA delivery.

patents.title: Antibodies Specifically Targeting CLDN6 and Their Use in the Preparation of CAR-T Cells
patents.abstract: Provided are an antibody specifically targeting CLDN6 and a use thereof in the preparation of a CAR-T cell. The provided CLDN6 antibody specifically targets CLDN6, but does not recognize CLDN3, CLDN4, or CLDN9 or exhibits significantly different recognition methods. A sequence of the antibody specifically targeting CLDN6A can be used to construct a chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) and a bivalent antibody (bispecific antibody). The CAR constructed on the basis of the sequence of the antibody can be transduced into a T cell to create a CAR-T cell specifically targeting CLDN6, which can be used for treating solid tumors such as ovarian cancer.
patents.assignee: SHENZHEN HAOSHI BIOTECHNOLOGY CO LTD [CN]; 深圳豪石生物科技有限公司
patents.novelty_summary: The patent presents a CLDN6-specific antibody with high selectivity (non-cross-reactive with CLDN3, CLDN4, CLDN9) and its application to construct CAR-T cells targeting CLDN6+ solid tumors, particularly ovarian cancer. This offers competitive advantage through improved specificity to reduce off-target toxicity in CAR-T therapy against claudin-6-expressing malignancies.
patents.title_original: ANTICORPS CIBLANT DE MANIÈRE SPÉCIFIQUE CLDN6 ET SON UTILISATION DANS LA PRÉPARATION D'UNE CELLULE CAR-T

patents.title: Means and methods for administration of agents to immune effector cells
patents.abstract: The present invention relates to functional delivery of nucleic acid to (resting) T-cells of mRNA and DNA, i.e. delivery resulted in translation from the mRNA and/or allowed for integration and/or expression from the delivered DNA. This delivery is achieved using nanoparticles, carrying a targeting moiety binding a T-cell, and, another moiety activating a T-cell. Preferably lipid nanoparticles are used, and advantageous compositions provided. These aspects of the invention, provide for highly efficient delivery of nucleic acid to T-cells, including resting T-cells. The nanoparticle technology thus provided herein allows for highly advantageous medical treatments, wherein a (human) patients whole blood can be treated (e.g. ex vivo), or wherein a patient can be administered with nanoparticles such as described directly into the bloodstream, therewith effectively delivering nucleic acid encoding therapeutic genes of interest to resting T-cells.
patents.assignee: NANOCELL THERAPEUTICS HOLDINGS B V [NL]; NANOCELL THERAPEUTICS HOLDINGS B.V.
patents.novelty_summary: This patent presents a novel nanoparticle-based delivery system combining a T-cell targeting moiety with a T-cell activation moiety to achieve functional nucleic acid delivery (mRNA translation and/or DNA integration/expression) to resting T cells. The competitive significance for in vivo CAR-T lies in enabling direct ex vivo or in vivo genetic modification of patient blood without prior T-cell activation, potentially streamlining CAR-T manufacturing and reducing processing time while improving transduction efficiency of quiescent T cells.
patents.title_original: MOYENS ET MÉTHODES D'ADMINISTRATION D'AGENTS À DES CELLULES EFFECTRICES IMMUNITAIRES

patents.title: Cancer Vaccines
patents.abstract: The invention relates to combinations for treating or preventing cancer comprising a closed linear DNA molecule and an mRNA molecule. The invention also relates to a closed linear DNA molecule and an mRNA molecule for use in a heterologous prime-boost immunization regimen in a subject. In addition, the invention relates to methods and kits incorporating and/or using the closed linear DNA molecule and the mRNA molecule.
patents.assignee: 4BASEBIO UK LTD [GB]; NEOMATRIX S R L [IT]; 4BASEBIO UK LTD
patents.novelty_summary: The invention combines closed linear DNA molecules with mRNA molecules in a heterologous prime-boost immunization regimen for cancer treatment/prevention. The competitive significance lies in the dual-modality approach using engineered DNA and mRNA to potentially enhance anti-tumor immune responses through sequential immunization, which differs from single-modality CAR-T or conventional gene therapy approaches.
patents.title_original: VACCINS CONTRE LE CANCER

patents.title: ENGINEERED IMMUNOCYTOKINES, FUSION POLYPEPTIDES, AND IL10 POLYPEPTIDES
patents.abstract: Provided are engineered heterodimeric immunocytokines, including fusions of IL4 and IL10, IL4 and IL13, or IL10 and IL13 to the heavy chains of an Fc fragment. In addition, fusion polypeptides are provided that comprise an engineered monomeric IL10 and a second cytokine. Also provided are engineered monomeric IL10 polypeptides with rearranged helices, for example, with an A helix joined to an F helix, in which a C-terminus of the D helix is not joined to an N-terminus of the E helix.
patents.assignee: SYNERKINE PHARMA B V [NL]; Synerkine Pharma B.V.
patents.novelty_summary: The patent discloses engineered heterodimeric immunocytokines with novel Fc-fusion architectures (IL4/IL10, IL4/IL13, IL10/IL13 fused to Fc heavy chains) and engineered monomeric IL10 polypeptides with rearranged helical structures. These immunocytokine designs aim to modulate immune responses through enhanced cytokine signaling, potentially relevant for redirecting T cell function in cellular immunotherapy contexts, though direct CAR-T application is not explicitly stated.

patents.title: LIPID NANOPARTICLE-BASED DRUG DELIVERY SYSTEM USING RECOMBINANT PROTAMINE AND METHOD FOR PREPARING SAME
patents.abstract: The present invention relates to a lipid nanoparticle-based drug delivery system using recombinant protamine and a method for preparing same. The lipid nanoparticle-based drug delivery system of the present invention can stably deliver a gene to a target cell in vivo by using a recombinant protamine protein having excellent stability when forming a complex with an anionic gene. In addition, the lipid nanoparticle-based drug delivery system can improve the expression level of the gene in the target cell, and thus can be effectively used in related technical fields such as lipid nanoparticle-mediated gene therapy.
patents.assignee: MOOGENE MEDI CO LTD [KR]; MOOGENE MEDI CO., LTD.
patents.novelty_summary: The invention presents a lipid nanoparticle (LNP) delivery system incorporating recombinant protamine to complex with anionic genes, offering improved stability and enhanced in vivo gene expression. This addresses a key challenge in LNP-based gene therapy by providing a protein-based complexation strategy that could enhance delivery efficiency and therapeutic outcomes for in vivo applications including CAR-T therapies.

patents.title: Ionizable cationic lipids with restricted structure and lipid nanoparticles
patents.abstract: Se describen lípidos catiónicos ionizables, métodos para sintetizar los mismos, intermedios útiles en la síntesis de los lípidos catiónicos ionizables y métodos para sintetizar los intermedios. Los lípidos catiónicos ionizables son útiles como componente de nanopartículas lipídicas (LNP), que a su vez pueden usarse para el suministro de ácidos nucleicos a las células in vivo o ex vivo. También se describen composiciones de LNP, que incluyen LNP que comprende un lípido funcionalizado para permitir la conjugación de una entidad de unión, y LNP dirigida (tLNP), que es una LNP en la que se ha conjugado una entidad de unión con el lípido funcionalizado y puede servir como una entidad de direccionamiento para dirigir la tLNP a un tejido o tipo celular deseado.
patents.assignee: CAPSTAN THERAPEUTICS INC [US]; CAPSTAN THERAPEUTICS, INC.
patents.novelty_summary: The patent describes novel ionizable cationic lipids with restricted structures and their use in lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) for nucleic acid delivery. Competitive significance for in vivo CAR-T therapy lies in the development of targeted LNPs (tLNPs) with functionalized lipids enabling conjugation of binding entities for cell-type or tissue-specific targeting, which could enhance CAR-T cell engineering and ex vivo CAR-T production while improving safety profiles.
patents.title_original: Lípidos catiónicos ionizables restringidos y nanopartículas lipídicas

patents.title: COMPOSITION FOR CELLULAR IMMUNOTHERAPY AND METHOD
patents.abstract: A chimeric receptor having an anti-transplant rejection function, an engineered cell expressing the chimeric receptor, an anti-tumor and anti-transplant immune rejection method, and in particular an anti-NK cell immune rejection method. Also provide is a cell therapy.
patents.assignee: CARSGEN LIFE SCIENCES CO LTD [CN]; Carsgen Life Sciences Co., Ltd.
patents.novelty_summary: The patent describes engineered cells expressing chimeric receptors with dual functionality targeting both anti-tumor and anti-transplant rejection responses, with specific emphasis on anti-NK cell immune rejection mechanisms. This represents a novel application of CAR technology beyond traditional tumor targeting, potentially addressing graft-versus-host disease (GVHD) or transplant rejection scenarios, which could expand CAR-T utility in solid organ and allogeneic transplant settings.
patents.title_original: ZUSAMMENSETZUNG FÜR ZELLULÄRE IMMUNTHERAPIE UND VERFAHREN

patents.title: PROGRAMMED CELL DEATH LIGAND 1 (PD-L1) TARGETING POLYPEPTIDE, MOLECULAR IMAGING PROBE, AND USE THEREOF
patents.abstract: A programmed cell death ligand 1 (PD-L1) targeting polypeptide, a molecular imaging probe, and a use thereof are provided. The PD-L1 targeting polypeptide includes any one of the following polypeptides: (1) a polypeptide shown in at least one of SEQ ID NO: 1 to SEQ ID NO: 9; and (2) a polypeptide that is derived from an amino acid sequence of (1) through a substitution and/or a deletion and/or an addition of one or more amino acid residues and has the same function as the amino acid sequence. The magnetic resonance molecular imaging probe based on the PD-L1 targeting polypeptide enables the early diagnosis and evaluation of a tumor and an immune-mediated myocardial injury.
patents.assignee: PEKING UNION MEDICAL COLLEGE HOSPITAL CAMS [CN]; Peking Union Medical College Hospital, Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences
patents.novelty_summary: The patent discloses PD-L1 targeting polypeptides (SEQ ID NOs 1-9 and variants) conjugated to magnetic resonance imaging contrast agents for molecular imaging. The competitive significance for in vivo CAR-T is limited; however, PD-L1 targeting moieties are relevant to CAR-T engineering as PD-L1 is an immune checkpoint that can be incorporated into CAR-T design or used diagnostically to monitor CAR-T activity and tumor microenvironment status.

patents.title: FUSION PROTEIN CONTAINING CAS PROTEIN AND BACTERIAL TOXIN AND USE THEREOF
patents.abstract: [0000]    A fusion protein may include a Cas protein and a bacterial toxin. Such a fusion protein, a polypeptide thereof, and/or a CRISPR-Cas system including the fusion protein may allow effective base editing. Due to the small size of the polypeptide, the polypeptide can facilitate delivery through vectors. In addition, when indels are accordingly induced, indel efficiency can significantly increase, and for indel induction, the size of nucleotides where indels are formed can also increase, whereby effective utilization can be made for gene knock-out.
patents.assignee: THE ASAN FOUND [KR]; UNIV OF ULSAN FOUNDATION FOR INDUSTRY COOPERATION [KR]; RESEARCH & BUSINESS FOUNDATION SUNGKYUNKWAN UNIV [KR]
patents.novelty_summary: A fusion protein combining a Cas protein with a bacterial toxin domain to improve base editing efficiency and indel induction while reducing molecular size for enhanced vector delivery. This approach is significant for gene therapy applications requiring efficient gene knockout with improved delivery kinetics, particularly relevant for ex vivo T cell engineering where delivery optimization is critical.

patents.title: COMPANION DIAGNOSTIC TO MONITOR THE EFFECTS OF GENE THERAPY
patents.abstract: [0000]    The invention relates to the field of gene therapy. In addition the invention relates to the field of interfering RNA and/or microRNA (miRNA). In particular the invention relates to gene therapy involving such miRNA's and more in particular to diagnostic tools to be implemented in the treatment of disease, when such treatment is carried out by delivery of miRNA's to a patient, i.e. to cells of a patient. The present invention uses the content of extracellular vesicles that are found in body fluids to determine the presence of miRNA's or the like expressed through the introduction of a gene delivery vehicle is in a host.
patents.assignee: UNIQURE IP B V [NL]; uniQure IP B.V.
patents.novelty_summary: The patent describes a diagnostic method using extracellular vesicles (EVs) in body fluids to monitor miRNA expression following gene therapy delivery. The competitive significance lies in enabling non-invasive, real-time monitoring of therapeutic gene delivery efficacy and tissue distribution, which is valuable for clinical development and patient stratification in gene therapy programs.

patents.title: TARGETING VECTOR, PREPARATION METHOD THEREFOR AND USE THEREOF
patents.abstract: [0000]    Provided are a targeting vector and a method for targeting same to a host cell. The vector comprises a first molecule that binds to an endocytosis receptor of the target cell and a second molecule that promotes the release of a substance carried by the targeting vector into a cytoplasm. When the targeting vector is a viral vector, the first molecule is not part of a viral envelope protein, and the second molecule promotes endosomal escape or lysosomal escape of the targeting vector. The first molecule is designed according to the endocytosis receptor of the cell to be targeted, different types of cells can be targeted, and after a reasonable mutation is carried out on the vector, infection of cells that do not need to be targeted can be avoided, thereby improving the accuracy of the vector.
patents.assignee: SHENZHEN GENOCURY BIOTECH CO LTD [CN]; SHENZHEN GENOCURY BIOTECH CO., LTD.
patents.novelty_summary: The patent describes a targeting vector platform with modular first and second molecules for receptor-specific cell targeting and endosomal/lysosomal escape, designed to improve targeting accuracy and reduce off-target transduction. For in vivo CAR-T applications, this could enable more precise viral delivery of CAR constructs to target T cells while minimizing transduction of non-target cell populations, potentially improving CAR-T manufacturing efficiency and reducing systemic toxicity.

patents.title: Single-domain antibody inhibitor of TNFR2 and its use
patents.abstract: Disclosed are an inhibitory TNFR2 single-domain antibody and a use thereof. The antibody comprises CDR regions having certain sequence identity to the amino acid sequences shown in SEQ ID NOs: 2-4. The inhibitory TNFR2 single-domain antibody can effectively inhibit the binding of a TNF to TNFR2. Moreover, the antibody also has the effects of reducing the proportion of Treg cells and inhibiting the proliferation of Treg cells. In addition, the molecular weight of the antibody is only one tenth of that of a traditional antibody. The antibody can also effectively penetrate the blood-brain barrier while effectively reducing production costs and difficulty. Compared with the traditional antibody, the antibody has greater potential in the treatment of TNFR2-related diseases.
patents.assignee: UNIV OF MACAU [CN]; RESEARCH INST OF TSINGHUA PEARL RIVER DELTA [CN]; 澳门大学
patents.novelty_summary: A single-domain antibody (sdAb) targeting TNFR2 that inhibits TNF-TNFR2 binding while reducing regulatory T cell (Treg) proportion and proliferation. The sdAb's reduced molecular weight (~1/10 of conventional antibodies) enables superior blood-brain barrier penetration and lower manufacturing costs, with significant potential for treating TNFR2-related diseases including cancer immunotherapy applications.
patents.title_original: ANTICORPS À DOMAINE UNIQUE INHIBITEUR DE TNFR2 ET SON UTILISATION

patents.title: Modified viral particles for targeted administration
patents.abstract: Provided herein, among other things, are novel and improved glycoproteins, including modified glycoproteins; engineered viral particles comprising such novel and modified glycoproteins; and methods for targeted delivery, for example, to immune cells such as T cells. In some aspects, the engineered viral particles allow targeted delivery of the cargo for various applications, including treating various conditions such as autoimmune diseases and cancer. In some aspects, the engineered viral particles comprise a viral fusogen that is a glycoprotein of Chandipura, Perinet, Piry, Jurona viruses, or variants thereof. In other aspects, the engineered viral particles comprise a modified vesiculovirus glycoprotein mutant, for example, with mutations at amino acids corresponding to positions I347 or R354 of Vesicular Stomatitis Virus G (VSV-G) that reduce binding to Low Density Lipoprotein Receptor (LDL-R).
patents.assignee: ORBITAL THERAPEUTICS INC [US]; ORBITAL THERAPEUTICS, INC.
patents.novelty_summary: The patent discloses engineered viral particles with modified glycoproteins (including Chandipura, Perinet, Piry, Jurona virus glycoproteins and vesiculovirus mutants) designed for targeted delivery to immune cells, particularly T cells, with applications in cancer and autoimmune disease treatment. The competitive significance lies in the use of pseudotyped or engineered viral vectors as delivery vehicles for CAR-T cell engineering and gene therapy, offering improved specificity and transduction efficiency compared to conventional lentiviral or retroviral approaches.
patents.title_original: PARTICULES VIRALES MODIFIÉES POUR ADMINISTRATION CIBLÉE

patents.title: PHARMACEUTICAL COMPOSITION FOR SUBCUTANEOUS ADMINISTRATION CONTAINING HUMAN HYALURONIDASE PH20 VARIANT AND DRUG
patents.abstract: The present invention relates to a pharmaceutical composition including (a) a drug and (b) a human PH20 variant. The human PH20 variant included in the pharmaceutical composition according to the present invention comprises amino acid residue substitution(s) in one or more regions selected from an alpha- helix 8 region (S347 to C381) and a linker region (A333 to R346) between alpha-helix 7 and alpha-helix 8 in wild-type human PH20 having the amino acid sequence of SEQ ID NO: 1, wherein amino acid residue(s) located at the N-terminus or the C-terminus is(are) selectively truncated. In addition, the pharmaceutical composition according to the present invention may further comprise a pharmaceutically acceptable additive, particularly a stabilizer. patents.novelty_summary: The invention describes a pharmaceutical composition containing a engineered human PH20 hyaluronidase variant with specific amino acid substitutions in alpha-helix 8 and linker regions, combined with a drug for subcutaneous delivery. The PH20 variant is designed to enhance subcutaneous bioavailability and absorption of co-administered therapeutics, offering competitive advantage for improving delivery of large biologics and cell therapies via non-intravenous routes.

patents.title: ZOMIB-BASED NANOMICELLAR FORMULATION AND PREPARATION METHOD THEREFOR
patents.abstract: Provided are a zomib-based nanomicellar formulation and a preparation method therefor. The nanomicellar formulation comprises: carfilzomib, a micelle carrier material, and a stabilizer, wherein the mass ratio of carfilzomib, the micelle carrier material, and the stabilizer is 1:15-30:15-30, and the carrier material is PEG-DSPE. PEG-DSPE is used as a drug carrier to prepare a carfilzomib micelle formulation. The formulation has a particle size of 8-20 nm, has high entrapment efficiency, and has a strong cell penetration capability without being quickly cleared. In addition, the preparation process is simple, without requiring lyophilization. Compared with existing cafilzomib formulations, the toxicity is reduced at the same dosage.
patents.assignee: JIANGSU BIOSCENE PHARMACEUTICAL CO LTD [CN]; 江苏百奥信康医药科技有限公司
patents.novelty_summary: A nanomicellar formulation of carfilzomib (proteasome inhibitor) using PEG-DSPE as carrier with optimized mass ratios (1:15-30:15-30), achieving 8-20 nm particles with high entrapment efficiency and reduced toxicity compared to existing formulations. While not directly a CAR-T technology, this represents an improved drug delivery platform potentially applicable to ex vivo CAR-T manufacturing or in vivo conditioning regimens, where proteasome inhibitors are used to enhance CAR-T persistence and reduce exhaustion.
